The agent SHALL retain it in the conversation\n45\t  or, at its discretion, in a temporary location outside the repository.\n46\t  It SHALL NOT be persisted in the repository. The agent chooses whether a\n47\t  temporary file is needed and, if so, its filename and format.\n48\t\n49\t**Actions:**\n50\t\n51\t1. Read the change request and existing clarifications.\n52\t2. Draft one statement describing the observable result for the intended\n53\t   human, agent, or system. Include the conditions under which it is needed.\n54\t3. Present the statement to the requester. When the proposed scope is also\n55\t   clear, present its inclusions, exclusions, and constraints in the same\n56\t   exchange. Obtain confirmation of both before drafting dependent definitions.\n57\t4. Ask the requester to resolve any missing information or competing\n58\t   interpretations that would change the outcome.\n59\t5. Revise the statement using the feedback. Repeat the exchange until the\n60\t   requester confirms the wording. Reuse an existing confirmation of the\n61\t   same wording.\n62\t6. Retain the confirmed statement and the confirmation as transient working\n63\t   material.\n64\t\n65\t**Harness command:** None.\n66\t\n67\t**Completion:** One intended-outcome statement is confirmed by the requester\n68\tand available for the following steps. It supplies the outcome for a missing intent (INT) drafted\n73\tin [Draft any missing definitions](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#draft-any-missing-definitions) or an amendment proposed in [Propose any needed amendments to existing definitions](AMEND_DEFINITIONS.md#propose-any-needed-amendments-to-existing-definitions). Any lasting definition belongs\n74\tin those formal artifacts.\n75\t\n76\t### Define the limits of the change\n77\t\n78\t**Inputs:** The confirmed outcome from [Describe the intended outcome](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#describe-the-intended-outcome) and the constraints supplied\n79\tby the requester.\n80\t\n81\t**Output:**\n82\t\n83\t- **Formal artifacts:** None created or modified.\n84\t- **Transient working material:** The confirmed scope statement and requester\n85\t  clarification. List the behaviors, components, and interfaces included in the change.\n90\t2. List the adjacent behaviors, components, and interfaces excluded from it.\n91\t3. Present these boundaries to the requester. Identify any unresolved boundary.\n95\t6. Revise the scope until the requester confirms it. No unresolved boundary affects the\n105\tdefinitions to be drafted next.\n106\t\n107\t**Later use:** The scope selects artifacts in [Identify the existing artifacts that apply to the change](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#identify-the-existing-artifacts-that-apply-to-the-change), limits definition work\n108\tin [Draft any missing definitions](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#draft-any-missing-definitions), [Propose any needed amendments to existing definitions](AMEND_DEFINITIONS.md#propose-any-needed-amendments-to-existing-definitions), [Define how the result will be verified](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#define-how-the-result-will-be-verified), and supplies the work order (WO) boundaries in [Prepare work orders (WO) linking the definitions, scope, planned work, and verification requirements](DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements).\n109\t\n110\t### Identify the existing artifacts that apply to the change\n111\t\n112\t**Inputs:** The confirmed outcome, scope limits, any artifact IDs supplied\n113\tin the request, and the existing formal records. The agent\n122\t  SHALL retain them in the conversation or, at its discretion, in a temporary\n123\t  location outside the repository. They SHALL NOT be persisted in the\n124\t  repository. The agent chooses whether a temporary file is needed and, if\n125\t  so, its filename and format.\n126\t\n127\t**Actions:**\n128\t\n129\t1. Run the repository inspection command below.\n130\t2. If the request selects a work order (WO), run the selected-work command\n131\t   below. Read that work order (WO) and every file in the returned\n132\t   `context.reading_manifest`.\n133\t3. Otherwise, locate the artifacts named in the request. If none are named,\n134\t   use `docs/engineering/README.md` to locate the domain covering the function\n135\t   or component in the scope. For each selected artifact, retain its name and code, such as Requirement\n145\t   (REQ), its ID, file path, current lifecycle state, and why it applies to the\n146\t   change. These records explain why a change is\n5\tneeded, what it must do, who may carry it out, and how its result is checked.\n6\t\n7\tArtifacts use TOML metadata between `+++` markers. Links are recorded in the\n8\t`[relations]` table using artifact IDs. A filename, a shared directory, or a\n9\tmention in prose does not create a formal link.\n10\t\n11\tThe tables below describe artifact types and permitted links. They are not a\n12\tmanually maintained list of the repository's actual artifacts. `harnessctl`\n13\treads those artifacts and checks their links and lifecycle states.\n14\t\n15\t## Artifact types\n16\t\n17\t“Required” means the selected work needs coverage of that type. It does not\n18\tmean every change must create a new file. Reuse an existing active artifact\n19\twhen its accepted meaning and scope still cover the work. Create a conditional\n20\tartifact only when its condition applies.\n21\t\n22\tFor an existing selected work order (WO), get its current state and next\n23\taction with:\n24\t\n25\t```text\n26\tharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --json\n27\t```\n28\t\n29\tBefore implementation, check whether that work order (WO) and its linked\n30\tdefinitions are eligible to start:\n31\t\n32\t```text\n33\tharnessctl preflight REPO --work-order WO-ID --phase start --json\n34\t```\n35\t\n36\tThe first command reports lifecycle context without evaluating checkpoint\n37\tgates. The second evaluates start readiness, including the states and coverage\n38\tof the selected definitions. Neither command approves or starts work.\n39\tHere, `REPO` is the absolute repository path and `WO-ID` is the actual ID of\n40\tthe selected work order (WO). Use the repository's selected released evaluator.\n41\t\n42\t| Type                  | ID prefix | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                      | When needed                                                                                                                                              |\n43\t|-----------------------|-----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\n44\t| `intent`              | `INT-`    | States the problem, intended outcome, and limits of responsibility.                                                                                                          | The work needs an accepted purpose. Reuse an intent (INT) when that purpose still applies.                                                               |\n45\t| `capability`          | `CAP-`    | Describes an ability that a human or agent should have.                                                                                                                      | Requirements (REQ) need a link to the capability (CAP) they support.                                                                                     |\n46\t| `requirement`         | `REQ-`    | States required behavior or a constraint, with a condition for acceptance.                                                                                                   | The change creates or changes an obligation. Reuse a requirement (REQ) only if its meaning stays unchanged.                                              |\n47\t| `specification`       | `SPEC-`   | Defines the detailed behavior, interfaces, constraints, and rejection conditions.                                                                                            | Each requirement (REQ) selected for implementation needs specification (SPEC) coverage.                                                                  |\n48\t| `architecture`        | `ARCH-`   | Defines system structure and boundaries needed to meet significant requirements (REQ).                                                                                       | An active architecture (ARCH) directly addresses a requirement (REQ) selected by the work order (WO).                                                    |\n49\t| `adr`                 | `ADR-`    | Records an architecture decision (ADR), the alternatives, and their consequences.                                                                                            | An applicable architecture (ARCH) declares that a significant decision is required.                                                                      |\n50\t| `verification`        | `VER-`    | Defines how requirements (REQ) will be checked and what counts as a pass.                                                                                                    | Each selected requirement (REQ) needs verification coverage. This is the verification contract (VER), not a test result.                                 |\n51\t| `work_order`          | `WO-`     | Defines the bounded work to execute and its governing artifacts. Approval grants work authority.                                                                             | Before execution. One work order (WO) may cover several requirements (REQ). Completed scope does not authorize later work.                               |\n52\t| `verification_record` | `VREC-`   | Binds work orders (WO), verification contracts (VER), evidence, and one exact candidate commit for assessment.                                                               | When verification tied to a commit is required. One record may cover several work orders (WO) at the same commit.                                        |\n53\t| `release_contract`    | `REL-`    | Defines permitted release scope, gates, rollback conditions, and authority limits.                                                                                           | When a release record (RLS) is proposed.                                                                                                                 |\n54\t| `release_record`      | `RLS-`    | Records preparation and the later release decision for verified work at one exact commit.                                                                                    | When a formal release is proposed. Preparing the record does not release the work.                                                                       |\n55\t| `decision`            | `DEC-`    | Records a question, options, recommendation, decision maker, affected artifacts, and the eventual answer. It can also record a deviation from one specification (SPEC) rule. | A question blocks a transition, affects more than one artifact, or must remain recorded after approval; or work cannot meet a specification (SPEC) rule. |\n56\t| `risk`                | `RISK-`   | Records a threat, an owner, and a next action. Scoring and categories are optional.                                                                                          | A concern needs follow-up. A separate decision (DEC) is used when the concern must block work.                                                           |\n57\t| `operating_contract`  | `OPS-`    | Defines continuing service, support, monitoring, or operational assurance obligations.                                                                                       | Ongoing operational commitments apply. Omitting the record does not prove those commitments have been met.                                               |\n58\t\n59\tCode, tests, acceptance scenarios, evidence files, commits, dashboards, tickets,\n60\tand conversations are not additional formal artifact types. They may support\n61\tor be referenced by formal artifacts but do not grant authority by themselves.\n62\t\n63\t## Artifact locations\n64\t\n65\tNew formal artifacts use these directories below\n66\t`docs/engineering/DOMAIN/`. `DOMAIN` is the selected domain name. These paths\n67\tdescribe storage, not authority; the artifact ID, metadata, and typed links\n68\tremain authoritative. Use the supported authoring command to obtain the actual\n69\tpath. Do not move existing records merely to match this table.\n70\t\n71\t| Artifact | TYPE | Directory |\n72\t| --- | --- | --- |\n73\t| Intent (INT) | `intent` | `intent/` |\n74\t| Capability (CAP) | `capability` | `capabilities/` |\n75\t| Requirement (REQ) | `requirement` | `requirements/` |\n76\t| Specification (SPEC) | `specification` | `specifications/` |\n77\t| Architecture (ARCH) | `architecture` | `architecture/` |\n78\t| Architecture decision (ADR) | `adr` | `architecture/adr/` |\n79\t| Verification contract (VER) | `verification` | `verification/` |\n80\t| Work order (WO) | `work_order` | `work-orders/` |\n81\t| Verification record (VREC) | `verification_record` | `verification-records/` |\n82\t| Release contract (REL) | `release_contract` | `release/` |\n83\t| Release record (RLS) | `release_record` | `releases/` |\n84\t| Operating contract (OPS) | `operating_contract` | `operations/` |\n85\t| Decision (DEC) | `decision` | `decisions/` |\n86\t| Risk (RISK) | `risk` | `risks/` |\n87\t\n88\tThe same domain has `evidence/` for retained work-order evidence and\n89\t`acceptance/` for acceptance scenarios. These are supporting files, not new\n90\tformal artifact types. Legacy flat artifact locations remain readable and\n91\tMUST NOT be moved by an upgrade without separate authority.\n92\t\n93\tTemplates under `docs/engineering/templates/` are authoring assets. These links describe meaning and coverage, not execution order.\n7\t\n8\tRepository validation, draft validation and work-order preflight share the\n9\tdeclared source/relation/target types. A supplied undeclared relation or a target\n10\tof the wrong type is invalid even when no work order selects the artifact.\n11\tPreflight still evaluates readiness only for its selected governing chain.\n12\tThe read-only draft query permits specific unfinished authoring slots; ordinary\n13\tvalidation and approval retain their completeness requirements.\n14\t\n15\t```mermaid\n16\tflowchart LR\n17\t    CAP[\"Capability (CAP)\"] -->|derives_from| INT[\"Intent (INT)\"]\n18\t    REQ[\"Requirement (REQ)\"] -->|derives_from| CAP\n19\t    SPEC[\"Specification (SPEC)\"] -->|specifies| REQ\n20\t    VER[\"Verification contract (VER)\"] -->|verifies| REQ\n21\t    ARCH[\"Architecture (ARCH)\"] -->|addresses| REQ\n22\t    ARCH -->|conforms_to| SPEC\n23\t    ADR[\"Architecture decision (ADR)\"] -->|decides| ARCH\n24\t```\n25\t\n26\t| Source → target | Relation | Meaning and coverage |\n27\t| --- | --- | --- |\n28\t| Capability (CAP) → Intent (INT) | `derives_from` | Each active capability (CAP) names one or more active intents (INT). |\n29\t| Requirement (REQ) → Capability (CAP) | `derives_from` | Each active requirement (REQ) names one or more active capabilities (CAP). |\n30\t| Specification (SPEC) → Requirement (REQ) | `specifies` | Each requirement (REQ) selected by a work order (WO) needs one or more selected active specifications (SPEC). |\n31\t| Architecture (ARCH) → Requirement (REQ) | `addresses` | The architecture (ARCH) names every requirement (REQ) that materially drives its structure. |\n32\t| Architecture (ARCH) → Specification (SPEC) | `conforms_to` | For each addressed requirement (REQ), the selected architecture (ARCH) names at least one selected specification (SPEC) covering it. |\n33\t| Architecture decision (ADR) → Architecture (ARCH) | `decides` | Each selected architecture (ARCH) that requires a design decision has at least one selected active architecture decision (ADR). |\n34\t| Verification contract (VER) → Requirement (REQ) | `verifies` | Each selected requirement (REQ) has one or more selected active verification contracts (VER). |\n35\t\n36\t## Declared links\n37\t\n38\tOnly links declared in formal TOML metadata establish\n39\ttraceability. Every link MUST use one of the relation names and source/target\n40\ttype pairs in this file, [Work and evidence](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#links-from-work-orders-wo), and [Decisions and risks](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#links-for-decisions-and-risks). Run `harnessctl validate REPO --json` to check those links.\n41\tTreat a reported undeclared pair as a validation failure; correct the link before the affected action.\n42\t\n43\t## Architecture applicability\n44\t\n45\tInclude an architecture (ARCH) only when it\n46\tdirectly addresses a selected requirement (REQ) and is active.   "content": "1\t# Artifact Authoring\n2\t\n3\tThe key words **MUST**, **MUST NOT**, **REQUIRED**, **SHALL**, **SHALL NOT**,\n4\t**SHOULD**, **SHOULD NOT**, **RECOMMENDED**, **NOT RECOMMENDED**, **MAY**, and\n5\t**OPTIONAL** in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14\n6\t(RFC 2119 and RFC 8174) when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.\n7\t\n8\t## Purpose and precedence\n9\t\n10\tThis policy guides authoring, design and review. Templates and skills point\n11\there; `harnessctl create-artifact` prints the selected type's checklist.\n12\tThe shared principles and questions are maintained here.\n13\t\n14\tIt ranks below the machine contracts, approved formal semantics, and the\n15\tworkflow, decision-right, quality-gate, and traceability policies, and above\n16\ttemplates, skills, prompts, and model prose. It grants no authority: a\n17\tchecklist item is a review standard, not an approval. Rules marked\n18\t*mechanical* are enforced by the validator or a gate; the rest are judgement\n19\trules for the accountable reviewer.\n20\t\n21\t## Design simplicity\n22\t\n23\tFor unfinished work, `harnessctl validate-draft REPO --artifact ID --json`\n24\treports whether one supported draft has an admissible shape. Only exact values\n25\tat the same type and field in this evaluator's canonical template, and missing\n26\tor empty required authoring links, can be reported as incomplete. Invalid\n27\tidentity, dates, metadata shapes, actual endpoints, lifecycle history and\n28\tdisposition are errors. A missing non-template ID is an error. Background\n29\tfindings remain visible; this result makes no whole-repository validity claim.\n30\tComplete the authoring checklist and pass ordinary approval gates before\n31\trequesting approval. Draft admission grants no authority to write or approve.\n32\t\n33\tChoose the least complex design that satisfies the agreed requirements and\n34\tconstraints. Justify material added complexity by the need it serves and why\n35\ta simpler approach is insufficient. Consider the effort to understand, build,\n36\ttest, operate and change the whole solution. Defer speculative needs. Review\n37\tboth the necessity of the specified behavior and the simplicity of its\n38\timplementation. Preserve correctness and the project's required quality and\n39\tsafety properties.\n40\t\n41\tStart from the smallest complete solution. Each project supplies its agreed\n42\tusers, scale, operating conditions and quality constraints. Agreed future needs\n43\tcan matter; imagined flexibility alone is insufficient. Credible risk analysis\n44\tcan justify prevention before an incident. Fewer lines, shorter specifications\n45\tor fewer tests do not establish simplicity; moving work to users, operations\n46\tor dependencies also has a cost.\n47\t\n48\tApply the relevant questions below before definition approval and during design\n49\tand implementation review. Return unjustified obligations or design complexity\n50\tfor revision through the existing decision process. Explain material choices\n51\tin the existing specification, design or review: the need, why a simpler option\n52\tis insufficient and the added cost. Scale the explanation to the decision; a\n53\tsmall choice may need one sentence, a significant design may use its existing\n54\tarchitecture decision. Trivial changes need no separate comparison document.\n55\t\n56\tThese are human review standards. They introduce no separate KISS artifact,\n57\tmandatory score, receipt, automated simplicity gate or additional approval.\n58\t\n59\t## requirement\n60\t\n61\t### Checklist\n62\t\n63\t- State the observable behavior and why it is needed. Ordinary language is accepted; `SHALL` is optional.\n64\t- What agreed outcome does this obligation serve, for whom and under which conditions? Separate requirements from assumptions and speculative needs.\n65\t- Include a concrete acceptance condition in `Examples`, `Acceptance`, `measure`, `verification_notes`, or a linked verification contract.\n66\t- Name the source capability and a verification method. Supported method arrays contain `test`, `analysis`, `inspection`, or `demonstration`; retained text methods remain readable.\n67\t- Replace unfinished placeholders and resolve blocking decisions before approval.\n68\t\n69\t### Guidance\n70\t\n71\tWrite enough for someone to implement and check the behavior. Use the template's\n72\tsections when helpful. Word counts, sentence shapes and numbers of code references\n73\tare not checked. Writing hints never block approval. Optional metadata must still\n74\thave a valid value when supplied.\n75\t\n76\t## intent\n77\t\n78\t### Checklist\n79\t\n80\t- Explain the present problem, who it affects, and the outcome wanted.\n81\t- What is the smallest useful outcome, and which needs and constraints are actually agreed?\n82\t- Say how the owner will know the change helped; an honest baseline may be `not measured`.\n83\t- State the important scope limits. Create a new intent when the desired outcome changes.\n84\t\n85\t## capability\n86\t\n87\t### Checklist\n88\t\n89\t- Say what an actor should be able to do and any relevant conditions.\n90\t- Does each supported case serve an agreed need under those conditions?\n91\t- Link the intent it serves. The graph lists the derived requirements.\n92\t- Put implementation details where they help the implementer; no required `can ... under` wording.\n93\t\n94\t## specification\n95\t\n96\t### Checklist\n97\t\n98\t- Explain what an implementation must do, including meaningful failure behavior.\n99\t- Is each promised behavior necessary? Could a simpler contract meet the agreed need? Prescribe a mechanism only when it is a necessary constraint.\n100\t- Link the requirements and show an example someone can check.\n101\t- Give a rule a stable identifier when evidence or a decision needs to refer to it.\n102\t- Check that supplied rule references exist and identifiers are unambiguous.\n103\t\n104\tMissing summaries and ambiguous rule references may produce draft hints. Hints\n105\thelp a reviewer; they do not withhold approval. Existing approved text need not\n106\tbe rewritten to adopt these checklists.\n107\t\n108\t## architecture\n109\t\n110\t### Checklist\n111\t\n112\t- `addresses` names only architecturally significant requirements; `conforms_to` names the specifications it must respect.\n113\t- Components, responsibilities, dependency direction, and trust boundaries are each stated.\n114\t- The decision assessment is complete: `adr_required` with triggers, or `no_significant_decision` with a rationale.\n115\t- For material added complexity, what simpler approach was considered, including existing capabilities? Explain why it is insufficient and the added cost across development, testing, operation and change.\n116\t\n117\t## adr\n118\t\n119\t### Checklist\n120\t\n121\t- Context, drivers, at least two considered options with consequences, the decision, and its consequences.\n122\t- The chosen option is stated as a decision, not a preference.\n123\t- If the chosen option adds material complexity, why is the simpler option insufficient for the agreed constraints, and is the added cost justified?\n124\t- Every `decides` target architecture is an active artifact.\n125\t\n126\t## verification\n127\t\n128\t### Checklist\n129\t\n130\t- Independence: expected values derive from the requirements and specifications, never from candidate output.\n131\t- A requirement-to-evidence matrix with a pass condition per requirement.\n132\t- Cover normal behavior and meaningful failure outcomes or risks; do not invent failure scenarios to fill a template.\n133\t- What accepted behavior or quality does each test or CI check establish? Cover distinct relevant outcomes, reuse applicable evidence, and avoid mirroring every implementation branch or combination.\n134\t- Pass criteria name the platforms and the evaluator.\n135\t\n136\t## work_order\n137\t\n138\t### Checklist\n139\t\n140\t- `[execution_scope].paths` is exact: files or component-prefix directories, nothing wider.\n141\t- `[assurance]` is classified and its rationale names what later decisions depend on.\n142\t- In scope and out of scope are both stated; the decision envelope says what the implementer may and may not decide.\n143\t- Stop conditions and the completion report format are stated.\n144\t- Is every planned change needed for the agreed outcome? Include removal or adjustment of obsolete behavior, tests and instructions within the approved scope.\n145\t- Inspect supporting paths before approval and assess the supplied plan through [Draft work orders](harness/DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements). Keep reasons in Expected change surface; do not add a separate planning artifact.\n146\t\n147\t## Review of implemented changes\n148\t\n149\t- Does the result satisfy the necessary contract, and did implementation reveal unnecessary specified behavior? Resolve an excessive approved obligation through the existing amendment process before changing its behavior.\n150\t- Is each material addition needed? Could a direct solution or existing capability meet the same constraints with less total work to understand, test, operate and change?\n151\t- Does the normal design or review evidence explain significant complexity and its cost? Remove unused generality or indirection that has no agreed purpose.\n152\t- Do tests and CI establish the accepted behavior and relevant quality properties? Remove obsolete checks together with the obligations they no longer serve.\n153\t\n154\tRetain material findings and their resolution with the ordinary review evidence.\n155\tApplying these questions is part of that review, not a second review or receipt.\n156\t\n157\t## release_contract\n158\t\n159\t### Checklist\n160\t\n161\t- `gates` names every work order the release may include.\n162\t- Version, rollback conditions, and evidence expectations are explicit.\n163\t\n164\t## operating_contract\n165\t\n166\t### Checklist\n167\t\n168\t- `assures` names every requirement it claims continuing assurance for.\n169\t- Observability, support, and operating obligations are measurable.\n170\t\n171\t## decision\n172\t\n173\tA pending question becomes a `decision` (`DEC-`) when it blocks a transition\n174\tof another artifact, concerns more than one artifact, or must survive the\n175\tapproval of the artifact that raised it. Below that threshold the actor asks\n176\tand the answer stays in the transition's `reason`.\n177\t\n178\t### Checklist\n179\t\n180\t- `kind` is `question` (an ambiguity met while authoring or planning) or `deviation` (an implementation cannot meet one rule of one specification). *(mechanical)*\n181\t- One `question`, `raised_by`, at least two `[[options]]` with `id` and `label`, and a `recommendation` naming one option. *(mechanical)*\n182\t- A deviation also names `against = \"SPEC-xxx#PREFIX-AREA-NNN\"`, a rule identifier the specification defines *(mechanical: E-DCM-005)*, and the `observed` fact; its options are drawn from `amend`, `supersede`, `accept`, `stop` and include `stop`. *(mechanical)*\n183\t- `concerns` names every artifact the question is about; `blocks` names the artifacts that cannot change state while it is `open`, each also in `concerns`. *(mechanical)*\n184\t- The `[disposition]` table is written by `harnessctl decide`; a hand-written one is `E-DCM-003`. A deferral needs a scope and a revisit trigger; accepting a deviation needs a revisit trigger. *(mechanical)*\n185\t- `decided` and `withdrawn` decisions are never deleted or rewritten.\n186\t- The definition templates carry no `Open decisions` section: a definition's pending decisions are the `DEC-` artifacts that name it in `blocks`, and the approval gate reads them from the graph. A legacy section, where one remains, reads `None` or lists `DEC-` identifiers; prose there is `E-DCM-004`.\n187\t\n188\t## risk\n189\t\n190\t### Checklist\n191\t\n192\t- Record a description, an owner and a next action.\n193\t- Use `harnessctl raise-risk --description TEXT --action TEXT --owner ROLE` with a domain and title.\n194\t- Stage, category, threatened artifacts and scoring are optional. If scoring is useful, supply likelihood and impact together (1–5); the command computes their product.\n195\t- Request `--with-decision` only when the owner needs a decision that blocks named artifacts. A risk by itself does not block work.\n196\t- Keep earlier scores, decisions and dispositions as recorded; no migration is required.\n197\t\n198\t\n199\t## verification_record and release_record\n200\t\n201\tPrepared by `capture-verification` and `prepare-release`; they are not\n202\tauthored by hand. This policy does not apply to them.\n203\t"
