Run\n28\t`harnessctl COMMAND --help` for the exact parser help in the selected environment.\n29\tThe syntax inventory below shows parser defaults and optional inputs; always\n30\tsupply an absolute `TARGET` for repository operations from the external directory.\n31\t\n32\t## Command shape\n33\t\n34\tThese rules describe the local evaluator commands (`WO-ECP-022`).\n35\tThe unpublished hosted `remote` client has the separate contract below:\n36\t\n37\t- **The repository is the positional `TARGET`**, default `.`, on every\n38\t  command that reads or writes one. `select-work-order` reads an event file,\n39\t  `identity` reads a runtime environment and `qualify candidate-package`\n40\t  reads a wheel, so they take none. `skill-ownership` requires an explicit\n41\t  positional `TARGET` under SPEC-PLG-020; it has no implicit repository selection.\n42\t- **Naming.** `--artifact` selects an existing artifact; `--id` names the\n43\t  record a command creates; an option that names a relation of that record\n44\t  keeps the relation's name (`--work-order`, `--verification`,\n45\t  `--verification-record`, `--release-contract`). Both record commands name\n46\t  their preparation actor `--owner`. `preflight` keeps `--work-order`\n47\t  until it folds into `check`.\n48\t- **`--json` everywhere.** The workflow commands print the schema-2 result;\n49\t  `validate`, `validate-draft`, `inspect`, `resources`, `release-unit`, `identity`\n50\t  and `qualify` print their own objects; every other command prints one\n51\t  `se-harness-command-result-v1` object with the same facts as its human\n52\t  output.\n53\t- **Plan and write.** A command that changes existing governed state\n54\t  (`transition`, `decide`, `upgrade`, `skill-ownership`) plans by\n55\t  default and writes only with `--apply`. A command that adds content\n56\t  (`init`, `scaffold-domain`, `create-artifact`) writes by default and\n57\t  plans with `--dry-run`; `init` into a target with content appends the\n58\t  bounded fragments to existing files and refuses every other difference.\n59\t- **Exit codes.** `0`: completed. `1`: the command ran and its result is\n60\t  failed, blocked or not passing. `2`: the command could not run (a usage\n61\t  error, a refusal before any result). A failed result goes to standard\n62\t  output in both renderings; a code appears once per line.\n63\t\n64\t## Command inventory\n65\t\n66\t| Command | Principal actor | State effect | Intended use |\n67\t| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n68\t| `remote` | authorized sandbox operator or author; reader for reads | explicit remote reads or bounded sandbox draft writes; no local fallback | use the separately installed unpublished client; see [Hosted sandbox client](#hosted-sandbox-client-unpublished) |\n69\t| `init` | repository owner or authorized agent | writes the complete standard harness into an absent or empty target; into a target with content it preserves existing files, integrates the bounded fragments and writes `docs/engineering/ADOPTION_REPORT.md` | install the harness into any repository, new or existing |\n70\t| `validate` | human or agent | read-only | validate formal metadata, typed relations, lifecycle, coverage, evidence paths, and provenance |\n71\t| `validate-draft` | human or agent | read-only | inspect one supported draft, separating invalidity, unfinished authoring slots and background findings |\n72\t| `inspect` | human or agent | read-only | summarize existing validation, lifecycle queues, Explorer findings, and bounded next-step guidance without acting as a gate |\n73\t| `dashboard` | human or agent | writes derived output only | generate the read-only Harness Explorer; under `--json` an engine refusal exits 2 and a failed generation carries the engine's standard error in `error` |\n74\t| `resources` | human or agent | read-only | resolve instructions and templates from the selected external resource package; available since 0.21.0 and in the selected released 0.22.1 evaluator |\n75\t| `doctor` | human or agent | read-only | inspect installation integrity, required supplied files and evaluator identity |\n76\t| `preflight` | coding agent or reviewer | read-only | check one work order for start or review readiness and return its reading manifest |\n77\t| `evidence` | coding agent at a checkpoint | writes or rebinds one evidence packet header | write the work order's evidence packet with a machine header bound to the current formal snapshot, keeping the owner-authored body byte for byte |\n78\t| `pr-body` | coding agent opening a pull request | read-only | emit the LF-terminated pull-request body: the work-order line, the restitution line when a Git-derived handoff result is retained, and the evidence list; an unknown artifact is a failed result on standard output, exit 1, as for `check` and `evidence` |\n79\t| `check-pr` | managed GitHub CI | scope check; may rebind an in-progress handoff | check one or several approved work orders and their combined diff |\n80\t| `check` | human or agent selecting work or assessing a checkpoint | read-only, except the self-binding Git-derived handoff checkpoint, which rebinds the packet header and retains its completed result | without a checkpoint, return the selected artifact's complete execution context: state, governing chain, declared scope, reading manifest, next command and required decision, in one schema-2 result, selecting the single in_progress work order when none is named; with a checkpoint, evaluate one fixed checkpoint and emit canonical restitution |\n81\t| `transition` | authorized actor; a person or agent uses the same recorded WO approval for start and completion after local checks pass (see [one execution route](delegation-class.md)) | plan is read-only; `--apply` atomically mutates only explicitly selected artifacts | validate and record accountable lifecycle decisions without implicit related-record changes |\n82\t| `decide` | the human who holds `DR-DECISION-DISPOSE`, directly or under an explicitly named eligible owner label | plan is read-only; `--apply` writes the decision's `[disposition]` table and one lifecycle event, and moves every raised risk the decision concerns in the same act | answer, defer, or withdraw one open decision artifact so the artifacts it blocks can move again |\n83\t| `raise-risk` | anyone working: a reviewer, an implementer, or an agent mid-execution; no decision right is needed | writes one risk artifact in `raised`, and with `--with-decision` the open decision that blocks the threatened artifacts; dry-run is read-only | record one measured threat to governed work so that an owner answers it before the threatened stage moves |\n84\t| `risks` | human or agent | read-only | list the risks threatening one artifact and its governing chain, with score, state and pending decision |\n85\t| `select-work-order` | managed GitHub CI | read-only | select exactly one standalone work-order declaration from a bounded pull-request event through released package logic |\n86\t| `upgrade` | repository owner or explicitly authorized agent | plan is read-only; `--apply` mutates managed content transactionally | update an initialized/adopted repository after separately updating the package |\n87\t| `skill-ownership` | repository owner or authorized agent | preview is read-only; apply replaces disposable copies and saves the provider last | select plugin skills or restore repository skills; rerun after an interruption |\n88\t| `scaffold-domain` | coding agent | writes owner-controlled directories and a seed index; dry-run is read-only | create the canonical organization for one engineering domain |\n89\t| `create-artifact` | coding agent | writes one incomplete `draft`; dry-run is read-only | create a formal artifact from its canonical template and path mapping |\n90\t| `release-unit` | release owner or coding agent drafting a release contract | read-only | measure a release unit's work-order census from the commit trailers between the previous release tag and a candidate commit, and compare it with a contract (`E-CIP-001`) |\n91\t| `identity` | CI or advanced contributor | read-only identity report/check | prove released-evaluator, candidate-source, or candidate-package runtime origin and boundary |\n92\t| `qualify` | release CI, maintainer, or released evaluator | read-only except for one exclusive evidence output outside the inspected repository | run one of four fixed evaluator/target qualification roles and emit provenance-bound, non-authoritative evidence |\n93\t| `capture-verification` | coding agent after an authorized clean candidate | writes one `ready` VREC plus canonical evaluator evidence | bind selected work, verification contracts, evidence, evaluator identity, snapshot, and exact clean `HEAD` |\n94\t| `refresh-verification` | coding agent after an unchanged rebase | writes a new `ready` VREC | compare relevant Git entries and reuse evidence while preserving the original |\n95\t| `prepare-release` | coding agent after verification and release-preparation authority | writes one `ready` RLS plus canonical evaluator evidence | bind release policy, eligible VRECs, exact work coverage, released evaluator wheel identity, version, and the same candidate commit |\n96\t\n97\t## Hosted sandbox client (unpublished)\n98\t\n99\t`harnessctl remote` is available in candidate client 0.22.2, installed into a\n100\tseparate test environment. The selected released evaluator 0.22.1 does not\n101\tprovide this command. Keep the released evaluator selected for repository and server checks.\n102\t\n103\tIn these examples, `CLIENT_PYTHON` is the absolute Python path in the separate\n104\tcandidate environment. Run from outside the checkout. `HAG_TEST_TOKEN` is the\n105\tname of a private environment variable; do not put its value in the command.\n106\t\n107\t```text\n108\t\"CLIENT_PYTHON\" -I -m se_harness remote status --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:18080 --token-env HAG_TEST_TOKEN --json\n109\t\"CLIENT_PYTHON\" -I -m se_harness remote read --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:18080 --token-env HAG_TEST_TOKEN --project PROJECT_ID --baseline BASELINE_ID --request READ_REQUEST_JSON --json\n110\t```\n111\t\n112\tThe positional argument is an operation, not a repository path. Every operation\n113\trequires an explicit endpoint and credential-variable name. Operations other\n114\tthan `status` also require `--project`. `baseline` selects `--baseline`;\n115\t`operation` selects the original operation `--key`. `read`, `check`, and `query`\n116\tuse a versioned `--request` and an explicit baseline or context view.\n117\t\n118\tThe write operations are `import`, `draft-open`, `create-artifact`,\n119\t`revise-artifact`, and `freeze`. Each requires the complete versioned request\n120\tand `--client-wheel` identifying the actual separately installed candidate.\n121\tThere is no automatic retry, rebase, local fallback, or implicit apply step.\n122\tAfter an uncertain write, inspect its original operation key before retrying.\n123\t\n124\tThis client prints the remote protocol result, not the local evaluator result\n125\tschema. Transport errors go to standard error; an unknown write outcome is not\n126\ta refusal or proof that nothing changed. See the [hosted sandbox guide](hosted-artifact-graph.md)\n127\tfor the request contracts and qualification limits. These commands do not\n128\tapprove work, accept verification, or release artifacts.\n129\t\n130\t## Repository setup and inspection\n131\t\n132\t```text\n133\tharnessctl init [TARGET] [--project-name NAME] [--integration git|ci|pr] [--dry-run] [--json]\n134\tharnessctl validate [TARGET] [--json] [--advisories]\n135\tharnessctl inspect [TARGET] [--json] [--vocabulary-threshold N]\n136\tharnessctl dashboard [TARGET] [--output PATH] [--json]\n137\tharnessctl doctor [TARGET] [--json]\n138\t```\n139\t\n140\t`TARGET` defaults to the current directory. The successor candidate defaults to\n141\tthe two selection files, with no copied instructions, templates or adoption report.\n142\tRepeat `--integration` for explicit Git evidence attributes, CI/output ignores,\n143\tor a PR template. Installation resolves every destination before writing and\n144\trefuses conflicts and linked or escaping paths. Published 0.20.0 retains its\n145\trepository-copy behavior; these candidate options do not adopt a release.\n146\t\n147\tValidation reports deterministic errors and warnings but does not edit artifacts. Each finding names its assessment plane: `structure`, `governance`, configured `policy`, or non-blocking `maintenance`. Planes explain the finding source; they do not change severity, pass/fail behavior, or create a score.\n148\t\n149\tThe summary line carries a fourth number, `Advisories`. An advisory is a hint for the author of a draft requirement or intent (the `W-AUT-*` codes: statement shape, one obligation, length and budgets, the old free-text `verification_method`, the intent's outcome and success measures). It is not a warning: it is raised only while the artifact is `draft`, it is left out of the warning count and the plane counts, and it is listed only with `--advisories`. The JSON report always carries `advisories` and `advisory_count`. On a repository whose definitions are all approved, `Advisories: 0` is the normal reading. Since 0.18.0 the approval transition of a draft intent, capability, requirement or specification is refused while any advisory remains on it (`QGP-G1-AUTHORING`, `QGP-G2-AUTHORING`, `SPEC-TCM-007`); the refusal names each advisory and ends with `fix the draft and run the transition again`. `validate` itself keeps passing.\n150\t\n151\tInspection reuses the existing validator and Harness Explorer snapshot. It\n152\treports `mode = repository_wide`, no selected artifact, formal validity, ready\n153\tdecisions, draft definitions, active work, assurance preparation, and existing\n154\trepository findings. Human output groups repeated rule instances for\n155\treadability; `--json` retains every finding. Inspection output MUST NOT be used\n156\tas selected-iteration restitution.\n157\t\n158\tThe `assurance_pending` queue contains only an `implemented` work order whose explicit `[assurance]` classification is `required` and which has no direct `ready`, `verified`, or `released` VREC coverage. It suggests non-automatic preparation after one clean candidate commit; it does not select aggregate scope, create a record, or make the assurance decision. Completed legacy work without a classification and work explicitly classified `not_required` are not inferred into this queue.\n159\t\n160\tThe temporal reassessment observation `W-HEX-003` is deliberately narrow: it compares dates only for supported declared dependency relations whose source can still be meaningfully reassessed. It does not reopen completed work orders, reinterpret commit-bound verification or release records, or treat derived graph projections as declared dependencies.\n161\t\n162\tFor existing lifecycle queues and a closed set of actionable derived warning rules, inspection also reports deterministic suggested next steps. Each suggestion identifies its source, affected artifacts, action class, accountable role, and `automatic = false`. Suggestions contain no executable command and never assert eligibility or authority. Validator findings, informational observations, and unknown rules remain visible without guessed advice.\n163\t\n164\tInspection ends with a vocabulary section. It counts the words of every artifact's statement and body with code removed, drops common English and the harness terms the managed instructions define, and names the project terms at or above `--vocabulary-threshold` occurrences (default 50, between 30 and 100) that have no entry in `GLOSSARY.md` at the repository root, and the entries whose term appears in no artifact. The glossary is repository content. Published repository-copy installations seed it empty; minimal external-resource installation creates no glossary. Both routes preserve an existing glossary. The section is informational and never blocks.\n165\t\n166\tA successfully produced inspection exits zero even when formal validation failed or attention exists, so use `validate` when gate exit behavior is required. Inspection is repository-local derived evidence: it does not approve, authorize, verify, supersede, release, remediate, or independently govern the repository.\n167\t\n168\tDashboard defaults to `target/harness-dashboard/`; its generated files are derived evidence, not formal authority. The small `index.html` bootstrap verifies `dashboard-manifest.json`, then loads a summary, compact topology, readiness data, individual artifact details, and explicitly expanded evidence from digest-named static resources. Serve the directory from one HTTP origin, for example with `python -m http.server 8000 --directory target/harness-dashboard`; direct `file://` opening is intentionally rejected because progressive resource loading and integrity checks require an origin. Generation remains local and needs no application server, but publishing or sharing the directory exposes every manifest-declared artifact and evidence body; the command does not scan for secrets or redact repository material. Doctor checks the standard installed contract against `.engineering-harness.lock` and the current distribution.\n169\t\n170\t## Standalone draft validation\n171\t\n172\t```text\n173\tharnessctl validate-draft [TARGET] --artifact ARTIFACT-ID [--json]\n174\t```\n175\t\n176\tThe caller supplies a complete projection. The command uses one parsed catalog\n177\tand the executing evaluator's canonical templates. It writes nothing. JSON is\n178\t`se-harness-draft-validation-v1`, with `selection` (id, type, status, relative\n179\tpath), `admissible`, `errors`, `incomplete`, and `background`. Findings include\n180\tstable codes and structured field/relation/target details where relevant.\n181\tText reports the same facts. Exit 0 means admissible; 1 means a produced refusal;\n182\t2 means usage or a failure before a result can be produced.\n183\t\n184\tSupported draft types: intent, capability, requirement, specification,\n185\tarchitecture, adr, verification, work_order, release_contract and\n186\toperating_contract. Decision, risk, verification_record and release_record\n187\tcontinue through their existing commands.\n188\t\n189\tA requirement with `CAP-xxx`, an omitted `derives_from`, or an empty array can\n190\tbe admissible with an incomplete finding. A link to an existing release record,\n191\tan unknown non-template target, or `[\"CAP-xxx\", \"RLS-SEH-001\"]` is refused.\n192\tMalformed TOML and duplicate IDs block a trustworthy catalog globally. Other\n193\tunselected findings remain background. A correct endpoint does not establish\n194\treadiness of its full governing chain.\n195\t\n196\tSelection outside draft, lifecycle history and disposition are refused. This\n197\tsnapshot query cannot prove that imported identity or provenance is unchanged.\n198\tThe hosted caller must compare protected fields to its immutable base and enforce\n199\trights and expected versions. Admission does not waive validation, approval,\n200\tverification or release gates, and includes no lifecycle next step.\n201\t\n202\t<a id=\"released-resource-lookup-successor-candidate\"></a>\n203\t\n204\t## Released resource lookup\n205\t\n206\tReleased evaluators since 0.21.0 provide this command for repositories selecting\n207\tthe `released-resources-v1` layout. This repository uses independently installed\n208\t0.22.1 after explicit adoption under WO-HUP-030. Publication alone does not\n209\tchange a repository's selection.\n210\t\n211\t```text\n212\tharnessctl resources [TARGET] [--resource RESOURCE-ID] [--content] [--json]\n213\t```\n214\t\n215\tWithout `--resource`, list resource IDs, local paths, byte digests and headings\n216\tfrom the exact selected release. Use a returned ID with `--resource` to select\n217\tone item. `--content` requires that one ID; it does not return every guide at\n218\tonce. For `ENGINEERING_HARNESS.md`, it renders the project and selected version\n219\tin memory. No instruction copy or lifecycle state is written to the repository.\n220\t\n221\tJSON output uses `se-harness-resources-v1`, with the selected `release` identity\n222\tand `resources` array. Content requests also return `content` and\n223\t`content_sha256`. Missing, altered or mismatched selected resources cause a\n224\trefusal; the command does not install resources or borrow another release.\n225\t\n226\t## Work readiness\n227\t\n228\t```text\n229\tharnessctl preflight [TARGET] --work-order WO-... [--phase start|review] [--json]\n230\tharnessctl select-work-order --event GITHUB_EVENT_PATH [--json]\n231\t```\n232\t\n233\t`start` is the default phase. Preflight checks lifecycle eligibility, the governing chain, and the selected work order's explicit `[assurance]` declaration, then displays the classification, rationale, and deciding role with the reading manifest. A selected work order without a valid declaration fails even when completed legacy validation remains compatible. Passing proves structural readiness only; it does not prove comprehension, semantic scope fit, implementation correctness, the truth of the rationale or role claim, assurance, or release.\n234\t\n235\t`select-work-order` reads one bounded event file. A body uses either\n236\t`Harness-Work-Order: WO-AAA-001` or\n237\t`Harness-Work-Orders: WO-AAA-001, WO-BBB-002`. Use `--field work-orders`\n238\tfor one ID per output line. LF and CRLF are equivalent. Both declarations\n239\ttogether, duplicate IDs and malformed IDs are rejected.\n240\t\n241\t```sh\n242\tharnessctl check-pr [TARGET] --event EVENT.json --from-git BASE [--json]\n243\t```\n244\t\n245\t`check-pr` evaluates every selected approved work order and the complete diff\n246\tagainst their combined scope. Unrelated changes are not admitted by listing\n247\tanother work order; that work order must actually cover the path. In-progress\n248\twork also needs passing local handoff checks. CI calls this command directly.\n249\t\n250\t\n251\t## Selected-scope workflow execution\n252\t\n253\tThe command shapes below are stable interfaces. The candidate standard\n254\t[`CONTINUE.md`](../../templates/repository/standard/docs/engineering/harness/CONTINUE.md#continue-selected-work)\n255\troutes to the selected procedure, and\n256\t[`WORKFLOW.json`](../../templates/repository/standard/docs/engineering/WORKFLOW.json)\n257\tis the machine-readable contract loaded by `harnessctl`. Use the workflow rule\n258\tselected for the artifact's exact type, state, and direct related records. Do\n259\tnot derive a new transition or next action from this reference.\n260\t\n261\t```text\n262\tharnessctl evidence [TARGET] --artifact WO-... --checkpoint start|pre-action|transition|handoff \\\n263\t  [--rebound-at RFC3339] [--json]\n264\tharnessctl pr-body [TARGET] --artifact WO-... [--json]\n265\tharnessctl check [TARGET] [--artifact WO-...|VREC-...|RLS-...] [--json] [--include-background]  # without a checkpoint: the projection\n266\tharnessctl check [TARGET] --artifact WO-... --planned-path PATH [--planned-path PATH ...] [--json]\n267\tharnessctl check [TARGET] --artifact WO-...|VREC-...|RLS-... \\\n268\t  --checkpoint start|pre-action|transition|handoff|scope [--target STATE] \\  # with a checkpoint:\n269\t  [--procedure PROC-...] [--from-git BASE | --changed-path PATH ... \\\n270\t  [--changes-complete] | --change-manifest PATH] [--pull-request-body PATH] [--json]\n271\tharnessctl transition [TARGET] --set ID=STATUS --decision ID=ACTOR \\\n272\t  [--set ID=STATUS ...] [--decision ID=ACTOR ...] [--reason ID=TEXT ...] \\\n273\t  [--apply] [--json]\n274\t```\n275\t\n276\t`check` without `--checkpoint` is the one call an agent makes first (`WO-ECP-001`,\n277\tfolded from `next` by `WO-ECP-019`). It returns the projection of the selected artifact — the single\n278\t`in_progress` work order when `--artifact` is absent, otherwise `WEX-ECP-001` names the candidate\n279\tcount — with an additive `context` object: `reading_manifest` (the preflight manifest for the\n280\tphase the state implies, `start` for `approved` and `in_progress`, `review` afterwards),\n281\t`governing`, `declared_paths`, `state`, `next` (`argv`, `procedure_id`, `step_id`, the same step a\n282\tcheckpoint `check` selects) and `decision_required`. It writes nothing and needs no prior command.\n283\tThe human block renders the context as a `Context` section after `Command or response`, and\n284\t`result_sha256` binds it. The former `next` command was removed after 0.11.0 (`WO-ECP-020`); its\n285\ttombstone guard left with 0.15.0 (`WO-ECP-025`), so the parser now refuses the name as unknown.\n286\t\n287\t`check` without `--checkpoint` projects only the selected artifact's governing chain and direct\n288\tlifecycle dependencies. It uses the ordered recommendation registry in\n289\t`WORKFLOW.json`. For example, `WFL-WO-READY-VREC` takes precedence over\n290\t`WFL-WO-PREPARE-VREC`, so existing ready assurance coverage cannot produce a\n291\tduplicate-capture recommendation. Unrelated repository findings remain a\n292\tbackground count; `--include-background` expands categories without making\n293\tthem selected-scope work.\n294\t\n295\tThe optional `--planned-path` view assesses proposed files before approval.\n296\tIt requires an explicit work order and no checkpoint. Repeat the option for\n297\teach repository-relative file in the plan; the file need not exist yet.\n298\tExisting calls without this option are unchanged.\n299\t\n300\tThe schema-2 result adds `scope.preparation`: `planned_paths`, `coverage`\n301\t(`covered`, `uncovered` or `invalid`), `explicit_matches` with the matching\n302\t`scope_entry`, `automatic_matches` with the existing admission rule,\n303\t`uncovered_paths`, `invalid_declarations` and\n304\t`impact_analysis: \"not_assessed\"`. These machine fields participate in the\n305\tresult digest. The human report lists coverage and each path's reason.\n306\t\n307\tThe normal lifecycle projection, next action, exit meaning and gate fields\n308\tare preserved. **Exit zero does not mean the plan is covered.** Inspect\n309\t`scope.preparation.coverage` and resolve uncovered or invalid paths before\n310\trequesting approval. Coverage cannot prove that the agent found every\n311\taffected file. Planning writes nothing and does not populate actual changed\n312\tpaths, assert completeness, evaluate gates or authorize work.\n313\t\n314\tThe selected WO file and existing directly linked VREC/RLS records and their\n315\tdeclared evaluator evidence use their existing exact-path admission rules.\n316\tThe selected WO's own packet directory is reported separately under its\n317\texisting admission rule.\n318\tAn unallocated future record has no assessable path; explain its expected\n319\trelationship rule and check the actual destination after preparation.\n320\tOther review/log evidence needs explicit scope unless an existing rule covers\n321\tit. A neighboring file is not admitted by a generated record's directory.\n322\t\n323\tDo not combine planned paths with `--checkpoint`, `--target`, `--procedure`,\n324\t`--changed-path`, `--changes-complete`, `--change-manifest`, `--from-git`\n325\tor `--pull-request-body`. Invalid selection, malformed paths, case duplicates,\n326\tdirectory inputs and repository escapes are refused through normal diagnostics.\n327\tThis option must be used with a released evaluator that provides it; candidate\n328\tsource tests do not change the repository's selected evaluator.\n329\t\n330\tWith a checkpoint, `check` resolves the first matching rule, its typed `PROC-*` procedure, and its\n331\t`QG-*` gates; `--checkpoint scope` evaluates only the scope predicates of\n332\t`QG-G4-IMPLEMENTATION-EVIDENCE` for a work order in any lifecycle state and\n333\twrites nothing, which is what the managed pull-request gate runs (`WO-ECP-013`); [`harnessctl check` explained](harnessctl-check.md) walks\n334\tthrough the checkpoints, the rule table, the gates, and the refusal codes. `--checkpoint transition --target STATE` previews, read-only, the\n335\texact predicates and graph-structural checks `transition --set ID=STATE` will\n336\tevaluate (`WO-ECP-009`): the transition binding index of `QUALITY_GATES.json`\n337\tkeyed by artifact family and target state, evaluated by the same gate evaluator\n338\twith the same context, plus the `QGS-*` checks under the synthetic\n339\t`QG-STRUCTURAL` gate. A transition whose evaluation is not all `pass` renders\n340\t`Blocked by` with each refusing predicate's own identifier and writes nothing;\n341\tan applied transition that would be blocked fails closed with that identifier. `pre-action` requires `--procedure`, which must equal the selected\n342\tprocedure or one complete declared alternative. `--changed-path` may repeat;\n343\t`--changes-complete` asserts that the supplied set is complete, including an\n344\tempty set. The assertion is evidence, not proof from a trusted Git baseline.\n345\tWithout it, path-scope predicates are `not_assessable`.\n346\t\n347\t`--from-git BASE` derives the change set from Git instead of from typed\n348\tpaths: the union of `git diff --name-only BASE` against the working tree\n349\t(renames contribute both names) and the untracked files Git does not ignore,\n350\teach normalized as above; the set is complete by construction and the result\n351\trecords `change_set_source = \"git\"`. It is mutually exclusive with the\n352\tchanged-path options and the manifest (`WEX-ECP-002`); outside a Git\n353\tcheckout, with a base Git cannot resolve, or on any Git failure it blocks\n354\twith `WEX-ECP-003` and evaluates no predicate as `pass`. The selected work\n355\torder's own artifact file, written by its lifecycle transitions and so always\n356\tin the diff, is admitted to its scope by construction (`ECP-CHG-007`).\n357\t\n358\t`evidence` writes `DOMAIN/evidence/WO-ID/WO-ID-CHECKPOINT.md` (`WO-ECP-002`):\n359\ta fenced TOML header at byte offset 0 with exactly `artifact`, `checkpoint`,\n360\t`formal_snapshot_sha256` and `rebound_at`, followed by an owner-authored\n361\tbody. On an existing packet only the header bytes change; the body is\n362\tretained byte for byte, and a file without a header at offset 0, with a\n363\theader naming another artifact or checkpoint, or with invalid TOML is refused\n364\t(`WEX-ECP-010`). It refuses when a `.gitattributes` rule would convert the\n365\tpacket's line endings (`WEX-ECP-011`) and when the single `in_progress` work\n366\torder is not the one named (`WEX-ECP-012`). `QGP-G4I-EVIDENCE` reads that\n367\theader through a TOML parser; a packet without one is not assessable, and\n368\tthe message names the `evidence` command that writes the header (the\n369\tone-release substring grace closed under `WO-AUT-006`). `check --checkpoint handoff\n370\t--from-git BASE` is self-binding (`ECP-SBH-001` to `-006`): it rebinds an\n371\texisting packet header to the current formal snapshot before evaluating —\n372\tbody preserved, `evidence`'s `WEX-ECP-010`/`WEX-ECP-011` guards unchanged,\n373\tno packet created — and evaluates the change set with the retained result\n374\tpath included, so one run is the declared, digest-stable result. A\n375\tcompleted run retains its schema-2 result as `handoff.json` in the same\n376\tdirectory, written by the harness; that directory is admitted to the work\n377\torder's scope by construction.\n378\t\n379\t`pr-body` emits the pull-request body for an approved or later work order\n380\t(`WEX-ECP-014` otherwise): the standalone `Harness-Work-Order` line first, one\n381\tstandalone `Harness-Restitution` line carrying the retained `handoff.json`'s\n382\t`result_sha256` when it exists, then the seeded `## Summary` and\n383\t`## Verification` headings with every evidence path under the packet\n384\tdirectory. LF line endings only; the body round-trips through\n385\t`select-work-order` unchanged, so paste its output rather than typing it.\n386\t\n387\t`--change-manifest` is mutually exclusive with both changed-path options. It\n388\tmust be an in-repository UTF-8 JSON object containing only `schema` with value\n389\t`se-harness-change-set-v1`, Boolean `complete`, and ordered array `paths`.\n390\tPaths use `/`, exact-file or component-boundary directory-prefix matching, and\n391\treject absolute, traversal, backslash, wildcard, drive, URI, control-character,\n392\treserved-device, duplicate, and case-ambiguous forms.\n393\t\n394\t`check` always emits `se-harness-workflow-result-v2`. That structured result is\n395\tauthoritative. The deterministic direct human renderer uses `Outcome`, `Done`,\n396\t`Not done`, conditional `Blocked by`, `Current lifecycle state`, `Decision\n397\trequired`, `Next`, `Command or response`, and conditional `Alternatives` in\n398\tthat order. Exact-format consumers must use this renderer directly rather than\n399\task a model to transcribe it. `check`, `transition`, `capture-verification`,\n400\tand `prepare-release` emit the same `se-harness-workflow-result-v2` result\n401\tthrough one selector (`WO-ECP-005`); the former `--result-schema` option is\n402\tgone and passing it is an argument error. Each rule in `WORKFLOW.json` carries\n403\tonly the `done` and `current_lifecycle_state` prose of its restitution; the\n404\tnext step and the command come from the bound procedure.\n405\t\n406\tWhen `check` is blocked, `Next` and `Command or response` carry the corrective\n407\tform the contract declares for the first failing predicate: a command that\n408\tdiffers from the evaluated one (for example the handoff check with\n409\t`--changed-path` and `--changes-complete`), an escalation naming a decision\n410\tright, or a response describing the evidence to retain. The evaluated command\n411\tis never rendered as its own retry. Every schema-2 result carries\n412\t`result_sha256`. New results declare `digest_format = \"machine-fields-v1\"`\n413\tand hash stable machine fields rather than human wording. Retained results\n414\twithout the marker keep their original human-block digest; a pull-request body may declare it on one standalone\n415\t`Harness-Restitution:` line for CI to recompute. At `handoff`, a work order\n416\twhose `ready` verification record binds a commit no longer reachable from\n417\t`HEAD` is blocked with `W-ADS-002`; `--pull-request-body` additionally reports\n418\t`W-ADS-001` when the work-order trailer ends with a carriage return.\n419\t\n420\tAn agent-facing handoff may adapt wording, ordering, headings, and relevant\n421\texplanation or omit empty fields. It remains conforming only when it preserves\n422\tactual artifact IDs, outcome, observed effects, incomplete work, material\n423\tnon-effects, blockers, final lifecycle state, the accountable decision,\n424\tcommand argument boundaries or suggested-response meaning, and exactly one\n425\trecommended next action. Workflow-declared alternatives remain separate from\n426\tthat recommendation. Agent prose never becomes lifecycle authority.\n427\t\n428\t`transition` resolves IDs from formal metadata and plans by default. Each\n429\tselected ID needs one actor assertion. Rejection needs a non-empty reason; VREC\n430\tsupersession uses the reason as the exact successor VREC ID. A packet is\n431\tassessed as one proposed final graph. `--apply` rechecks every input byte,\n432\tproves the locked released-evaluator authority before writing, stages\n433\tsame-filesystem replacements outside artifact discovery, and rolls back earlier\n434\treplacements if a later write fails.\n435\t\n436\tThe command records actor text as an assertion, not proof of authority. The\n437\teffects and non-effects for each state are defined only by the matching\n438\t`WORKFLOW.json` rule. Related artifacts require separate explicit selection,\n439\tpassing gates, and authority.\n440\t\n441\tDirect human and JSON output are rendered from the same semantic workflow\n442\tresult. Schema 2 always identifies exactly one typed next step and derives its\n443\tcommand argument array or response from the selected procedure. Adaptive agent\n444\tpresentation consumes that result; it does not replace or recompute it.\n445\t\n446\t## Decision disposition\n447\t\n448\t```text\n449\tharnessctl decide [TARGET] --artifact DEC-... --option OPTION-ID --decision ACTOR [--authority-owner OWNER] --reason TEXT [--revisit TEXT] [--apply] [--json]\n450\tharnessctl decide [TARGET] --artifact DEC-... --defer --scope ARTIFACT-ID:FROM-TO ... --revisit TEXT --decision ACTOR [--authority-owner OWNER] --reason TEXT [--apply]\n451\tharnessctl decide [TARGET] --artifact DEC-... --withdraw --decision ACTOR [--authority-owner OWNER] --reason TEXT [--apply]\n452\t```\n453\t\n454\tA decision artifact (`DEC-`) records one pending question, or one implementation deviation from one rule of one specification. While it is `open`, every artifact named in its `blocks` relation is refused its transitions by the `QGP-*-DECISION` predicate of the gate that transition would pass. The refusal names the decision, its question, its options, the deciding role, and the `decide` command that clears it.\n455\t\n456\t`decide` is the only way a decision changes state; `transition` refuses it. Without `--apply` the command plans and reports; with `--apply` it writes the `[disposition]` table (the option, its label, the actual human, the time, and the verbatim reason) and one lifecycle event. `--option` must name one of the options the artifact declares. A deferral needs one `--scope` entry per transition it admits and a `--revisit` trigger; the scoped transitions pass, every other blocked transition still waits. Accepting a deviation needs `--revisit`, because acceptance is time-bounded. An ineligible owner is refused with `DR-DECISION-DISPOSE`.\n457\t\n458\t`--decision ACTOR` records the actual human who made the decision. With\n459\t`--authority-owner OWNER`, the evaluator checks OWNER against the existing\n460\tholders for the blocked artifacts, or the departed specification for a\n461\tdeviation. OWNER must match exactly and contain non-blank printable text of\n462\tat most 128 characters. It is retained separately as `authority_owner` in\n463\tthe disposition. Without the option, ACTOR must directly match a holder.\n464\tBoth preview and apply use the same checks. The CLI does not authenticate\n465\tthese claims or grant consent; the caller must first establish the human's\n466\tauthority and obtain the exact decision. Existing owner labels and historical\n467\trecords are not changed.\n468\t\n469\tThe validator reports a malformed decision as `E-DCM-001` to `E-DCM-003`, prose in a legacy definition's `## Open decisions` section as `E-DCM-004`, a deviation whose `against` fragment is not a rule identifier of the named specification (`SPEC-xxx#PREFIX-AREA-NNN`) as `E-DCM-005`, and an accepted deviation past its revisit or accepted twice against the same rule as `W-DCM-001` and `W-DCM-002`. See [decision artifacts](decision-artifacts.md) for the model.\n470\t\n471\tWhen the decision concerns a raised risk, `--apply` also moves that risk to the state the option names, in the same act: `accept` needs `--revisit`, `mitigate` needs `--mitigated-by WO-...`, and `avoid` records `--avoided-by` (an ADR or a decision; it defaults to the disposing decision). A deferral leaves the risk `raised`; a withdrawal withdraws it.\n472\t\n473\t## Risk recording\n474\t\n475\t```text\n476\tharnessctl raise-risk [TARGET] --domain SLUG --title TEXT --stage STAGE --category CATEGORY --cause TEXT --effect TEXT --likelihood N --impact N --threatens ID [--threatens ID ...] --raised-by ACTOR [--owner ROLE ...] [--id RISK-...] [--with-decision [--decision-id DEC-...] [--recommend accept|avoid|mitigate]] [--dry-run] [--json]\n477\tharnessctl risks [TARGET] --artifact ID [--json]\n478\t```\n479\t\n480\tA risk artifact (`RISK-`) records one measured threat: one cause, one effect, the stage it threatens, `likelihood` and `impact` from 1 to 5, and their product as `score`. `raise-risk` computes the score, writes the file in `raised` and records the raise as a lifecycle event, in one act; a measurement outside the range or an identifier already declared anywhere is refused before anything is written, exit 2. `--domain` takes the domain slug or the identifier token of exactly one domain. With `--with-decision` the command also writes the open decision that blocks the threatened artifacts, with the options `accept`, `avoid` and `mitigate`. No gate reads risks: the stop is the paired decision's `QGP-*-DECISION` predicate, and the refusal names the decision, not the risk.\n481\t\n482\t`risks` lists every risk threatening the named artifact or, for a work order, its governing chain; it writes nothing.\n483\t\n484\tThe validator reports a missing or invalid field as `E-RSK-001`, a wrong measurement or score as `E-RSK-002`, a raised risk that no pending decision names as `E-RSK-003`, a paired decision whose `blocks` differs from the risk's `threatens` as `E-RSK-004`, a disposition typed by hand as `E-RSK-005`, and an accepted risk past its revisit as `W-RSK-001`. See [risk artifacts](risk-artifacts.md) for the model.\n485\t\n486\t## Safe repository upgrade\n487\t\n488\t```text\n489\tharnessctl upgrade [TARGET] [--json]\n490\tharnessctl upgrade [TARGET] --apply [--json]\n491\tharnessctl upgrade [TARGET] --apply --work-order WO-... --evidence-output docs/engineering/DOMAIN/evidence/WO-...-evaluator-upgrade.json [--json]\n492\t```\n493\t\n494\tThe first form is a read-only plan. `--apply` is an explicit transactional repository mutation. Same-identity managed repair needs no new lifecycle packet. When the installed target evaluator differs from the standard lock, apply additionally requires a distinct approved or in-progress work order with an exact `[evaluator_upgrade]` packet and a work-order-keyed JSON evidence path. The packet binds the prior lock SHA-256 and exact immutable target archive/payload identity with `scope = \"standard-root-only\"`; a product release decision cannot substitute for it.\n495\t\n496\tApply requires the already-published target evaluator installed from exact wheel bytes outside the checkout, changes only eligible managed content, and stops without a partial managed update when identity, authority, customization, or conflict prevents a safe plan. Transition evidence, managed files, and the lock share the recoverable transaction, and successful replay must be a no-op. Every repository, including the `se_harness` implementation repository, follows this transaction and uses one exact released evaluator. GitHub discovers the managed workflow beside existing repository-owned workflows, while required-check and workflow-ordering policy remains external. See [installation and safe upgrades](harness-installation-and-upgrades.md).\n497\t\n498\t## Retained skill ownership\n499\t\n500\t```text\n501\tharnessctl skill-ownership TARGET --provider plugin --plugin-root DIRECTORY [--apply] [--json]\n502\tharnessctl skill-ownership TARGET --provider repository [--apply] [--json]\n503\t```\n504\t\n505\tThis candidate command is unavailable in released 0.17.0. It removes the two\n506\tnamed harness skill directories under .agents/skills and .claude/skills,\n507\tincluding edits and extra files. Other skill directories remain unchanged.\n508\tThe replacement must contain a Verity Plane manifest and the six required files.\n509\tPreview is optional. Apply reads current inputs, deletes the old copies, and\n510\tsaves the portable provider choice last. Rerun the command after an interruption.\n511\tRestoration copies the current repository templates over disposable old copies.\n512\tThis file-only operation grants no lifecycle authority and does not install a\n513\tplugin or change host settings. See [the current design](plugin-simplification-2026-09-13.md).\n514\t\n515\t## Predecessor-to-successor migration rehearsal\n516\t\n517\tThe former `rehearse-recovery` command is retired (`WO-ECP-030`, issue #376; it had no workflow caller and no retained report), as the former `rehearse-migration` command was (`WO-ECP-010`, issue #210); the root-evaluator handover is rehearsed by `python -m repository_tools.upgrade_rehearsal`, a repository-owned tool described in [rehearsing the root-evaluator handover](evaluator-migration-rehearsal.md), not by a `harnessctl` subcommand.\n518\t\n519\t\n520\t## Domain and artifact authoring\n521\t\n522\t```text\n523\tharnessctl scaffold-domain [TARGET] --domain DOMAIN [--title TITLE] [--dry-run] [--json]\n524\tharnessctl create-artifact [TARGET] --domain DOMAIN --type TYPE [--id ID] [--dry-run] [--quiet] [--json]\n525\t```\n526\t\n527\tDomain slugs, artifact identifiers, type prefixes, templates, and destinations are validated before mutation. `create-artifact` creates only an incomplete `draft`; it does not choose owners, relations, content, approval, or authority. After creation it prints the created type's checklist from `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`, resolved in the selected wheel for the external layout or in the repository for a supported older layout; `--quiet` suppresses it. Existing valid flat layouts remain discoverable and are not automatically migrated.\n528\t\n529\tWithout `--id`, `create-artifact` allocates the lowest free\n530\t`TYPE-DOMAIN-NNN` across every local branch and tag and the working tree,\n531\tuntracked files included (`WO-ECP-002`): the refs are enumerated with\n532\t`git for-each-ref` and each ref's `docs/engineering` tree is listed, so two\n533\tagents on two branches cannot take the same number; remote-tracking refs are\n534\tnot consulted. The domain token is read from the domain's existing\n535\tartifacts. The result names the refs on which the next-lower identifier was\n536\tfound, so a gap is explained. Outside a Git checkout allocation is refused\n537\t(`WEX-ECP-013`) rather than guessed from the working tree. An explicit `--id`\n538\tis refused when any local ref already carries it.\n539\t\n540\tNon-dry-run authoring uses the common pre-write mutation guard. The invoking environment must match the schema-3 released-evaluator identity locked by the target repository; candidate source and editable or contaminated installs fail without creating the requested path.\n541\t\n542\t## Release unit derivation\n543\t\n544\t```text\n545\tharnessctl release-unit [TARGET] --from TAG --to COMMIT [--exempt SHA ...] [--contract REL-ID] [--json | --toml]\n546\t```\n547\t\n548\tMeasures the work-order trailers between the previous release tag and a\n549\tcandidate commit, including merged work. The JSON shape remains compatible.\n550\tUntraced commits, incomplete census information, and contract differences are\n551\tadvisory and exit successfully; invalid Git refs or command inputs still fail.\n552\t`--exempt` remains readable for old invocations but is unnecessary. The owner\n553\tapproves final release scope, and the final candidate still needs verification.\n554\t\n555\t## Runtime identity\n556\t\n557\t```text\n558\tharnessctl identity --role released-evaluator|candidate-source|candidate-package \\\n559\t  --expected-version VERSION --expected-root PATH [options] [--json]\n560\t```\n561\t\n562\tKey role-specific options are `--checkout-root`, `--candidate-commit`, `--evaluator-wheel-sha256`, `--entry-point`, `--require-isolated-python`, and `--require-entry-point`. The command verifies declared runtime origin; it does not select an evaluator or approve a candidate.\n563\t\n564\tRuntime identity also observes the running interpreter's own entry-point path through the declared interpreter-safety rule and records three additional facts: whether the entry point is a symbolic link, which position class its resolved target occupies relative to the expected and checkout roots, and the target's SHA-256. The schema identifier stays `se-harness-runtime-identity-v3`, because consumers require a subset of the identity rather than an exact field set. The observation is recorded for every role, but only the two environment-bounded roles — `released-evaluator` and `candidate-package` — turn a refusal into the `RID024` diagnostic; `candidate-source` has no environment boundary, because its expected root is the checkout itself. `RID004` and `RID006` keep their existing meanings unchanged.\n565\t\n566\t## Role-specific release qualification\n567\t\n568\t```text\n569\tharnessctl qualify released-root [ROOT] [--output PATH] [--json]\n570\tharnessctl qualify complete-candidate [ROOT] --candidate-commit FULL_COMMIT [--output PATH] [--json]\n571\tharnessctl qualify candidate-package --candidate-wheel PATH --candidate-commit FULL_COMMIT --candidate-wheel-sha256 SHA256 --verifier-wheel-sha256 SHA256 [--checkout-root PATH] [--output PATH] [--json]\n572\tharnessctl qualify public-install [ROOT] --release-record RLS-... --public-wheel PATH --public-wheel-sha256 SHA256 --payload-sha256 SHA256 [--output PATH] [--json]\n573\t```\n574\t\n575\tThe four subcommands are separate closed parsers. They bind evaluator identity, target identity, fixed checks, and one independence class before reporting a result. They do not accept a general evaluator, validator, script, omission, or diagnostic-allowlist option. `--output` must name a new external file; the command never overwrites it or writes qualification evidence inside the inspected repository.\n576\t\n577\t`--evaluator-python` is judged by the declared interpreter-safety rule before anything is spawned. Supply the environment's own lexical entry point — `bin/python` on POSIX, `Scripts/python.exe` on Windows — not the resolved system interpreter it points at. The environment root is derived from that lexical path, so an interpreter reached through a linked or junctioned parent directory is refused, as is one inside the inspected checkout or whose resolved target lands inside it. The terminal interpreter link itself is permitted, which is what makes an ordinary `python -m venv` environment usable on POSIX.\n578\t\n579\tAll operations emit `se-harness-release-qualification-v1`. The result identifies the operation, completion, outcome, evaluator, target, ordered checks, independence boundary, and its evidence-only authority. `complete-candidate` is always `candidate-controlled`, even when it passes. See [release qualification roles](release-qualification-roles.md) for the workflow map. `WO-REB-028` retired a fifth operation, `predecessor-view`, with the predecessor-bootstrap release path; its `PV001` and `PV002` codes stay reserved and no code path emits them.\n580\t\n581\tThe pre-namespace `accept-candidate` entry point, kept as a one-cycle alias of `qualify\n582\tcandidate-package` under `REQ-REB-022`, was removed after 0.11.0 (`WO-ECP-019`); its tombstone guard left with\n583\t0.15.0 (`WO-ECP-025`), so the parser now refuses the name as unknown. Exact public 0.6.0 predates the `qualify` namespace;\n584\tits immutable command still emits `se-harness-functional-acceptance-v1` and is accepted only as\n585\texplicitly labeled bootstrap evidence in the candidate workflow's legacy branch, which runs only a\n586\tverifier without `qualify`. That historical output is not converted into or described as canonical\n587\tqualification evidence.\n588\t\n589\t## Commit-bound verification preparation\n590\t\n591\t```text\n592\tharnessctl capture-verification [TARGET] \\\n593\t  --id VREC-... \\\n594\t  --work-order WO-... \\\n595\t  --verification VER-... \\\n596\t  --evidence PATH \\\n597\t  [--owner ROLE] [--domain DOMAIN] [--output PATH] [--json]\n598\t```\n599\t\n600\tRefusals distinguish invalid state (`WEX301`), Git provenance (`WEX302`),\n601\tevidence (`WEX303`), and record inputs (`WEX304`). Repeat work orders, contracts,\n602\tand evidence paths for a final aggregate candidate. Work may be implemented,\n603\tverified, or released; all declared verification contracts must be selected.\n604\tEvidence may be a shared integration report plus earlier verification records.\n605\tThe command writes a ready VREC and evaluator evidence. It does not verify it.\n606\t\n607\tAfter WO-KIS-009, each selected WO's recorded execution approval and unchanged\n608\tscope authorize preparation for either a person or an agent. There is no\n609\tactor-specific single-WO limit. Use the installed evaluator's procedure on a\n610\trepository still governed by an earlier release until normal upgrade.\n611\tUse `--candidate-commit COMMIT --test-command <argv...>` to test the exact final\n612\tintegration in a temporary checkout, including when the caller has local edits.\n613\t\n614\tFor a harmless rebase, use\n615\t`harnessctl refresh-verification REPO --from VREC-OLD-001 --id VREC-NEW-001`.\n616\tThis compares relevant Git tree entries, governing inputs, and retained evidence.\n617\tIt preserves the old ready record and writes a new ready successor. Changed\n618\trelevant files require fresh tests; verified records cannot be refreshed.\n619\t\n620\tAn accountable assurance owner reviews the retained evidence and separately decides whether to transition the VREC to `verified`. The record lives in later governance history and continues to bind the earlier candidate commit C.\n621\t\n622\tIf a later verified or released VREC fully covers a prepared ready record, the assurance owner may instead apply the declared `ready -> superseded` transition and name that successor with `--reason`. The command preserves `prepared_at` and `prepared_by`, adds only the supersession decision fields, typed successor relation, lifecycle event, status, and update date, and does not add `verified_at` or `verified_by`. Supersession means the proposal was retired, not verified. Historical superseded VRECs without preparation fields may retain the older valid `verified_at` capture shape; validation does not rewrite them or fabricate `verified_by`.\n623\t\n624\t## Commit-bound release preparation\n625\t\n626\t```text\n627\tharnessctl prepare-release [TARGET] \\\n628\t  --id RLS-... \\\n629\t  --release-contract REL-... \\\n630\t  --verification-record VREC-... \\\n631\t  --work-order WO-... \\\n632\t  --version VERSION \\\n633\t  --owner ROLE \\\n634\t  [--tag TAG] [--domain DOMAIN] [--output PATH] [--json]\n635\t```\n636\t\n637\tThe corresponding release refusal codes are `WEX401` to `WEX404`. Select one\n638\tverified or released final-candidate VREC and repeat `--work-order` for the\n639\trelease scope. The final record must cover exactly that work and all its\n640\tverification contracts. The RLS binds its exact candidate commit. Earlier\n641\trecords may be cited as supporting evidence at different commits; passing\n642\ttheir individual checks cannot replace final integration verification.\n643\t\n644\tBefore writing, the command proves the locked released evaluator including its wheel filename and SHA-256. It writes canonical normalized evaluator evidence and binds the evidence path and digest in the `status = \"ready\"` RLS. The record contains `prepared_at` and `prepared_by`; it omits `released_at` and `authorized_by` until a separate release transition. For the external layout, explicitly select `--integration git` or establish an equivalent owner rule before evidence writes. The selected `.gitattributes` fragment applies exactly `docs/engineering/**/evidence/*.json text eol=lf`, preserving canonical evidence bytes across supported checkouts so the raw SHA-256 survives. Independent validation and publication replay reject missing, changed, noncanonical, candidate-role, host-path-leaking, or lock-mismatched evidence. A rejected contract can support only its exact rejected RLS as terminal history and remains invalid for preparation, binding, release, publication, or credential-bearing use. The command does not transition the record to `released`, commit, push, tag, create a GitHub Release, publish to PyPI, or deploy.\n645\t\n646\tOnly `ready` and `released` release records claim a version.     "content": "+++\nid = \"SPEC-P3-001\"\ntype = \"specification\"\ntitle = \"Fixed rehearsal greeting return value\"\nstatus = \"draft\"\nowners = [\"test-owner\"]\ncreated = \"2026-10-12\"\nupdated = \"2026-10-12\"\n# What an implementation must do to conform. The Explorer shows this summary under the title.\ncontract = \"The fixture function greeting() in src/greeting.py takes no arguments and returns the str value Hello rehearsal without external effects.\"\n\n[relations]\nspecifies = [\"REQ-P3-001\"]\n+++\n\n# Specification: Fixed rehearsal greeting return value\n\nSynthetic rehearsal input supplied by the test owner. This is not a real human decision.\n\n## In plain words\n\n`greeting()` always gives back the same fixed text, `Hello rehearsal`, and does nothing else.\n\n## Scope\n\nThis specification governs the return value and side effects of the function\n`greeting()` in `src/greeting.py`. The check method, platform and evidence\nlocation belong to the verification contract that verifies `REQ-P3-001`.\n\n## Terms\n\n- **Fixture function.** The function `greeting()` in `src/greeting.py` of the selected rehearsal source.\n\n## Rules\n\n**REH-GREET-001.** A call to `greeting()` with no arguments MUST return a value equal to the exact text `Hello rehearsal` (capital `H`, lowercase `rehearsal`, one ASCII space, no leading or trailing whitespace).\n\n**REH-GREET-002.** A call to `greeting()` MUST NOT read input, write output, or access the network or file system.\n\n## Failure behaviour\n\n| Trigger | Response | Diagnostic |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `greeting()` returns any value other than `Hello rehearsal` | The implementation does not conform to REH-GREET-001; an equality check reports failure | none |\n| `greeting()` raises an exception | The implementation does not conform to REH-GREET-001; the check reports failure | none |\n\n## Examples\n\n**Given** the selected fixture source, **when** a caller calls `greeting()`, **then** the result equals `Hello rehearsal` (REH-GREET-001).\n\n**Given** a changed fixture that returns `Hello Rehearsal`, **when** a caller calls `greeting()`, **then** the result does not equal `Hello rehearsal` and REH-GREET-001 is not met.\n\n## Coverage\n\n| Requirement | Rules |\n| --- | --- |\n| `REQ-P3-001` | REH-GREET-001, REH-GREET-002 |\n\n## Not decided here\n\n- The internal form of the implementation, such as a literal or a constant.\n"

Links to requirements (REQ) alone are not enough.\n7\t\n8\t| Source → target | Relation | Meaning and coverage |\n9\t| --- | --- | --- |\n10\t| Work order (WO) → Requirement (REQ) | `implements` | Names every requirement (REQ) in the authorized work scope. |\n11\t| Work order (WO) → Specification (SPEC) | `specifications` | Names the specifications (SPEC) governing those requirements (REQ). |\n12\t| Work order (WO) → Architecture (ARCH) or Architecture decision (ADR) | `architecture` | Names every applicable architecture (ARCH) and every required architecture decision (ADR). |\n13\t| Work order (WO) → Verification contract (VER) | `verification` | Names the verification contracts (VER) for the work. |\n14\t\n15\tFor example, a work order (WO) can declare these links in its metadata. The IDs\n16\tbelow are examples, not records created by this document.\n17\t\n18\t```toml\n19\t[relations]\n20\timplements = [\"REQ-EXAMPLE-001\"]\n21\tspecifications = [\"SPEC-EXAMPLE-001\"]\n22\tverification = [\"VER-EXAMPLE-001\"]\n23\t```\n24\t\n25\tThe referenced requirement (REQ) must also link back to a capability (CAP) and intent (INT).\n26\tAdd architecture (ARCH) links when architecture (ARCH) applies; do not invent them just to\n27\tfill a field.\n28\t\n29\t## Links for verification, release, and operation\n30\t\n31\t| Source → target | Relation | Meaning and coverage |\n32\t| --- | --- | --- |\n33\t| Verification record (VREC) → Work order (WO) | `verifies_work_order` | Names one or more work orders (WO) assessed at one exact candidate commit. |\n34\t| Verification record (VREC) → Verification contract (VER) | `conforms_to` | Names every verification contract (VER) required by those work orders (WO). |\n35\t| Verification record (VREC) → Verification record (VREC) | `superseded_by` | A superseded record names exactly one distinct eligible successor. |\n36\t| Release contract (REL) → Work order (WO) | `gates` | Names every work order (WO) the release contract (REL) permits the release to include. |\n37\t| Release record (RLS) → Release contract (REL) | `satisfies` | Names exactly one applicable release contract (REL). |\n38\t| Release record (RLS) → Verification record (VREC) | `includes_verification` | Names one or more eligible verification records (VREC) at the release's candidate commit. |\n39\t| Release record (RLS) → Work order (WO) | `releases_work` | Names exactly the combined set of work orders (WO) covered by the included verification records (VREC). |\n40\t| Operating contract (OPS) → Requirement (REQ) | `assures` | Names every requirement (REQ) covered by a continuing operational assurance claim. |\n41\t\n42\tA verification contract (VER) defines what to check. A verification record\n43\t(VREC) binds the evidence and work to an exact result for a later decision.\n44\tLikewise, a release contract (REL) defines the permitted release, while a\n45\trelease record (RLS) binds a particular release candidate and its decision.\n46\t\n47\t## Complete work scope\n48\t\n49\tEvery requirement (REQ) selected by a work order (WO)\n50\tMUST link back to active capabilities (CAP) and intents (INT). It MUST also\n51\thave selected active specifications (SPEC) and verification contracts (VER).\n52\tReuse existing artifacts where their scope applies.\n53\t\n54\tA work order should cover one complete bounded outcome, including its\n55\tforeseeable tests, documentation and retained evidence. A genuine expansion after approval\n64\tstill needs the applicable human decision; preserve the approved history.\n65\t\n66\t## Generated outputs\n67\t\n68\tExisting scope rules admit the selected work order's own file, records that\n69\tdirectly verify or release that work order, and those records' declared\n70\tevaluator-evidence paths. This does not admit those records' parent directories.\n71\tThe selected work order's own packet directory is also already admitted by\n72\tthe existing scope rules; the planning report identifies that separate rule.\n73\t\n74\tList other planned evidence, review and log destinations explicitly in the\n75\twork order's scope unless an existing rule covers them. A neighboring file\n76\tor a record linked only to another work order is not automatically admitted.\n77\tThe conditional rule for recording risks during execution remains unchanged;\n78\tit is not a blanket admission of future files during preparation.\n79\t\n80\tIf a future record's ID is not allocated, mark its destination as unresolved\n81\tand explain the relationship rule expected to cover it. Do not create a\n82\trecord or invent an ID to complete the plan. Once the evaluator prepares\n83\tthe record, assess its actual returned record and evidence paths. An\n84\tunresolved destination is not an already covered file.\n85\t\n86\t## Assurance classification\n87\t\n88\tEach work order (WO) in `approved` or\n89\t`in_progress` MUST set `assurance.commit_bound_verification` to `required`\n90\tor `not_required`.\n91\t\n92\tUse `required` when later decisions depend on the correctness of changes to\n93\tcode, required checks, CI configuration, harness policy, artifact definitions,\n94\tor their links. These are examples of “changed trusted state”: information or\n95\tbehavior that others will rely on when accepting, releasing, or operating the\n96\tresult.\n97\t\n98\tFor example, a work order (WO) changes the code that validates artifact links.\n99\tA later release decision relies on that validation being correct. The work\n100\torder (WO) therefore needs verification tied to its exact candidate commit.\n101\t\n102\tUse `not_required` only when the work solely records or transports a\n103\tverification, release, supersession, publication, or deployment decision\n104\tthat an authorized human has already made. It does not make a new decision\n105\tor change the definitions, implementation, or evidence behind that decision.\n106\t\n107\tFor example, a work order (WO) commits an already authorized release decision\n108\tin a release record (RLS), with no change to the released code, scope, or\n109\tsupporting evidence. The work records the decision; it does not reassess the\n110\trelease.\n111\t\n112\tA work order (WO) that combines both kinds of work MUST be split or classified\n113\t`required`. `not_required` removes the obligation to prepare a new\n114\tverification record (VREC) for that work; it does not remove required checks\n115\tor the links to verification contracts (VER).\n116\t\n117\t## Verification coverage\n118\t\n119\tA verification record (VREC) MUST bind one or more\n120\twork orders (WO), all their declared verification contracts (VER), retained\n121\tevidence, and one exact clean candidate commit. Preparing a verification\n122\trecord (VREC) does not change its state to `verified`.\n123\t\n124\t## Successor coverage\n125\t\n126\tA verification record (VREC) in `superseded`\n127\tkeeps its original commit, evidence, work orders (WO), and verification\n128\tcontracts (VER) unchanged. Its successor MUST be a different verification record (VREC) in\n129\t`verified` or `released`, covering every original work order (WO).\n130\tA verification record (VREC) in `superseded` MUST NOT qualify a release.\n131\t\n132\t## Release coverage\n133\t\n134\tA release record (RLS) MUST bind one release contract\n135\t(REL), one exact candidate commit, and eligible verification records (VREC)\n136\tat that same commit. Its released-work set MUST equal the combined set of\n137\twork orders (WO) covered by those verification records (VREC). Governance\n138\twork is included only when the release record (RLS) explicitly includes\n139\tverification records (VREC) that provide eligible coverage for that work.\n140\tA related record or dashboard cannot add work to a release.\n141\t\n142\tThis model describes the readable record structure. This release's\n143\t`prepare-release` procedure is narrower: it requires one final verification\n144\trecord covering the complete released-work set. When earlier records cover\n145\tseparate parts, prepare and verify a record for the exact combined candidate\n146\tthrough [Verify the outcome](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#procedure) before using that release procedure. Do not\n147\tassemble or edit a release record by hand to bypass the preparation checks.\n148\t\n149\t## Operational coverage\n150\t\n151\tAn active operating contract (OPS) assurance claim\n152\trequires an active requirement (REQ) and at least one completed work order\n153\t(WO) implementing it. Confirm the saved reason\\nin the resulting lifecycle entry before discarding the working notes.\\n\\nFor approval, `TARGET` is `approved`. For rejection, use `rejected` and add\\n`--reason \\\"ARTIFACT-ID=Rejection reason\\\"` to both commands. Rejection is\\nterminal. Correct incomplete or inconsistent draft content within the requested scope.\\n2. Return an accepted-definition change to the amendment procedure in\\n   \\u201cDefine the change.\\u201d Do not edit accepted authority to clear a check.\\n3. Add `--revisit \\\"Trigger\\\"` for acceptance of a\\ndeviation. A risk-mitigation option also requires `--mitigated-by WO-ID` for\\neach selected mitigating work order (WO). For a risk-avoidance option, use\\n`--avoided-by ARTIFACT-ID` when naming a separate architecture decision (ADR)\\nor decision (DEC). A decision right describes which\\naction that person or agent is authorized to perform. Being a Human does not\\ngrant every right in this table. Being an Agent grants none by itself.\\n\\nUse the artifact's recorded ownership and any existing explicit delegation to\\nidentify the accountable human. Resolve a team name or ownership label to the\\nhuman making this decision. A proposed `owners` value, an example actor name,\\nor authorship of a draft MUST NOT assign decision authority.\\n\\nApproval, verification acceptance, and release decisions MUST be made by an\\nauthorized human. An agent MAY prepare the material and apply that human's\\nrecorded decision when authorized to do so. Applying the decision does not\\nmake the agent its author. The selected IDs, reviewed content, target states,\\nand reason MUST still match the decision at apply time.\\n\\nThe following stable IDs name rights and operations, not additional profiles.\\nAll applicable gates remain required.\\n\\nThese DR-* identifiers come from the selected evaluator's decision-right\\ncatalogue. Use the right and exact action returned by that evaluator.                                               | Result                                                                                               |\\n|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `DR-DEFINITION-DECIDE`     | Human authorized to decide the selected definition.                                                                                | Complete definition, exact proposed state, and required checks.                                                   | Decision on that definition only.                                                                    |\\n| `DR-WO-SELECT`             | Human authorized to approve the work scope.                                                                                        | Complete governing chain, bounded work order, and assurance classification.                                       | Approval or rejection of the selected work order.                                                    |\\n| `DR-WO-START`              | Human or Agent executing the selected work under its recorded approval.                                                            | Unchanged approved scope and passing start checks.                                                                | The selected work order becomes `in_progress`.                                                       |\\n| `DR-WO-COMPLETE`           | Human or Agent executing the selected work under its recorded approval.                                                            | Completed scope, passing handoff checks, and retained evidence.                                                   | The selected work order becomes `implemented`.                                                       |\\n| `DR-VREC-PREPARE`          | Human or Agent under the approval of every selected work order.                                                                    | Exact candidate, selected work and verification contracts, retained evidence, and passing preparation checks.     | One `ready` verification record; no acceptance decision.                                             |\\n| `DR-VREC-DECIDE`           | Human authorized to accept verification for the selected candidate.                                                                | Ready record, assessed evidence, and the exact verify, reject, or supersede decision.                             | Decision on that verification record only.                                                           |\\n| `DR-DELIVERY-SELECT`       | Human authorized for the chosen integration or release-preparation path.                                                           | Exact candidate, destination, and coverage required by that path.                                                 | One path-specific instruction.                                                                       |\\n| `DR-RLS-PREPARE`           | Human authorizes the release inputs; a Human or Agent may carry out the preparation.                                               | Exact release contract, candidate, included work, verification coverage, version, and passing preparation checks. | One `ready` release record; no release decision.                                                     |\\n| `DR-RLS-DECIDE`            | Human authorized to make the release decision.                                                                                     | Ready release record, assessed contract obligations, and the exact release or reject decision.                    | Decision on that release record only.                                                                |\\n| `DR-EXTERNAL-ACTION`       | Human authorized for the exact external action. A Human or Agent may execute the authorized operation.                             | Action, immutable target, destination, prerequisites, and recovery conditions.                                    | Authorization limited to that operation; the subsequent tool result records its actual effects.      |\\n| `DR-RELATED-RECORD-SELECT` | Human or Agent; no decision authority is needed for inspection.                                                                    | Exact existing artifact ID.                                                                                       | Read-only selection.                                                                                 |\\n| `DR-REMEDIATION-SCOPE`     | Human authorized to change the affected definition or work scope.                                                                  | Failed criterion and proposed bounded correction.                                                                 | Explicit authority for the revised scope.                                                            |\\n| `DR-DECISION-DISPOSE`      | Human accountable for the artifact blocked by the decision; for a deviation, the human accountable for the affected specification. | Open or deferred decision, selected option or disposition, exact reason, and any required revisit trigger.        | Recorded disposition and any declared paired-risk effect. Other blocked artifacts keep their states. |\\n\\nFor a lifecycle decision, the `--decision` value identifies its actual\\ndecision-maker. When an agent applies a human decision, that value is the\\nhuman who made it. For start and completion under approved execution, it is\\nthe actual Human or Agent executor. Supplying either identity does not grant\\nauthority. Preparation `--owner` values identify the preparation actor, not\\na future assurance or release decision-maker.\\n\\nFor `decide`, when an owner label differs from the actual human's identity,\\nuse `--authority-owner OWNER` only after establishing that human's authority\\nfor the exact decision. Keep `--decision ACTOR` as the actual human. The\\nevaluator checks that OWNER holds the existing decision right and records it\\nseparately as `authority_owner`. With the option absent, ACTOR must itself\\nmatch an eligible owner. The command does not authenticate either claim or\\ngrant consent.
