A rejection MUST include a non-empty\\nreason. Supersession MUST name exactly one eligible successor. The decision\\nand its resulting state MUST remain specific to the selected artifact.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"6ecaeb29429bcaa4eac99857f2f921e270c4865d1edeec96f536d09eb6c3130a\"}, {\"heading\": \"delegation-and-separation\", \"title\": \"Delegation and separation\", \"anchor\": \"delegation-and-separation\", \"start_line\": 111, \"end_line\": 133, \"content\": \"## Delegation and separation\\n\\nA human decision right may be delegated only to another human who is permitted\\nto hold it. The delegation MUST name the right, its scope, the granting human,\\nand the receiving human. It MUST be recorded before the delegated decision.\\nThe receiving human MUST decide under their own identity.\\n\\nAn instruction for an agent to apply a recorded human decision delegates the\\nexecution of that command. It does not delegate the decision itself. The\\nagent MUST NOT supply a new answer, broaden the targets, or claim the human\\nmade a decision that was not given.\\n\\nRepository policy MAY require different people for conflicting decisions on\\nthe same candidate. When it does, the same human MUST NOT hold both decisions\\nfor that candidate. A human MUST NOT approve their own architecture decision\\nassessment unless they explicitly hold approval authority for that artifact\\nand the separation rules permit it. Drafting an assessment grants no such\\nright.\\n\\nWhen the accountable human or required authority is absent or ambiguous, stop\\nthe affected decision. State the exact right and artifact needing an owner.\\nDo not substitute an available human or agent merely to fill the field.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"f07389fbbe529ad544d8b7d7f18894bfa45f0ec69996c93ed8372416b55ddf91\"}, {\"heading\": \"authority-from-work-approval\", \"title\": \"Authority from work approval\", \"anchor\": \"authority-from-work-approval\", \"start_line\": 134, \"end_line\": 163, \"content\": \"## Authority from work approval\\n\\nWork-order approval authorizes execution of its approved scope: start,\\nimplementation, local edits and commits, required checks, evidence capture,\\ncompletion recording, and required verification-record preparation. A Human\\nand an Agent MUST use the same local approval, scope, and evidence checks.\\nContinue these operations without asking for the same permission again while\\ntheir scope and conditions still match. Record execution under the actual\\nexecutor's identity.\\n\\nApproval leaves the work order `approved` until its start transition is\\napplied. Selecting and scheduling work remain explicit. New approvals need\\nno separate execution delegation table or second start approval. A preliminary\\nmerge and live CI are not local execution requirements; CI still applies at\\nintegration and publication.\\n\\nThe grant does not include changed scope, acceptance of the result, release,\\nmerge, publication, or other external action. Reuse an existing explicit\\nauthorization for such an action only when its exact target and conditions\\nstill match.\\n\\nHistorical approvals keep their original meaning. Earlier explicit execution\\ngrants remain usable under the same scope checks. An older approval without\\nsuch a grant needs an authorized amendment for the remaining execution.\\nCurrent metadata or an actor label MUST NOT manufacture that historical grant.\\nIf the installed release cannot record the required authorization, stop the\\nremaining execution and report the missing historical grant and the lack of\\na supported amendment operation. Do not insert invented grant fields or\\nrewrite the old approval.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"a0ce00fccb8c1c8833455c14fe3ec75eaf01c597f0a1f46a24f7962ab1958f8c\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/RESULTS.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h44\\\\f\\\\claude-421\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\RESULTS.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"090e0172a78ebedfe4cdbe98e74c171e50215766a4ebbd671844a89af3f72e6e\", \"bytes\": 5242, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"read-this-when\", \"title\": \"Read this when\", \"anchor\": \"read-this-when\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 6, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Read this when\\n\\nReport a governed result, handle a refusal or recover an uncertain operation.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"680ff724251b96e21b52d9104a0e6f2806e6f4269237b555518e7d72d20463a7\"}, {\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nRead only the actual selected result and evidence needed to establish its effects. Before eligible English reporting, read [COMMUNICATION.md#communication](COMMUNICATION.md#communication) if it is no longer in context.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"22e8f880f3e2c5192c3f6abf5f63c7542b51647503ba0fb877c5acb70c7a5837\"}, {\"heading\": \"report-a-lifecycle-result\", \"title\": \"Report a lifecycle result\", \"anchor\": \"report-a-lifecycle-result\", \"start_line\": 13, \"end_line\": 46, \"content\": \"### Report a lifecycle result\\n\\nAfter a lifecycle stage completes or reaches a stop condition, obtain the\\nselected evaluator's schema-2 result. The result controls the reported scope,\\neffects, blockers, final state, required decision, alternatives, and next step.\\nThe human or agent MUST NOT recompute those fields.\\n\\nFor a human-readable report, lead with the outcome or required decision. The\\nwording and headings may vary, and empty fields may be omitted. The report\\nMUST preserve:\\n\\n1. The actual artifact IDs and whether the selected operation completed or\\n   was blocked.\\n2. The observed effects, separately from expected effects that did not occur.\\n3. Every exact blocker and every material non-effect. Confirm that all required evidence files exist at the locations named by\\n   the work order (WO) or verification contract (VER).\\n6. Run review preflight.\\n7. Apply [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#risk](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#risk) or [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#decision](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#decision) for the selected record.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e8a14639d6c2512ed5f9bfea0f7bfd9d4a2e428642e8fc8a02d600f792ab846f\"}, {\"heading\": \"record-risks-risk-affecting-the-change\", \"title\": \"Record risks (RISK) affecting the change\", \"anchor\": \"record-risks-risk-affecting-the-change\", \"start_line\": 13, \"end_line\": 65, \"content\": \"### Record risks (RISK) affecting the change\\n\\n**Inputs:** The outcome, scope, selected definitions, verification coverage,\\nand existing risks (RISK) found in [Identify the existing artifacts that apply to the change](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#identify-the-existing-artifacts-that-apply-to-the-change).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** New risks (RISK) in `raised` for threats not already\\n  covered. A paired decision (DEC) in `open` for each risk created with\\n  `--with-decision`. None created where existing records cover the threats.\\n- **Transient working material:** The selection of reused risks (RISK),\\n  review notes, generated IDs and paths, and links awaiting new work order\\n  (WO) IDs. If no risks are identified, retain that result with the reviewed\\n  scope. Retain this material under the same conditions as [Describe the intended outcome](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#describe-the-intended-outcome).\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Identify what could go wrong within the selected change scope.\\n2. Check whether an existing risk (RISK) already records each threat and its\\n   follow-up. Reference that record instead of creating a duplicate.\\n3. For each new risk (RISK), describe the threat and why it matters.\\n4. Identify its follow-up owner.\\n5. Specify the owner's next action.\\n6. Identify the formal artifacts threatened by it.\\n7. Determine whether an unresolved decision must block those artifacts.\\n8. Preview the risk (RISK) with the command below. Inspect the proposed\\n   content, affected IDs, and destination paths.\\n9. Run the same command with the same arguments, removing only `--dry-run`.\\n10. Read every written file reported by the command. Retain its ID and path\\n    for the review handoff.\\n\\n**Harness command:**\\n\\nReplace the quoted text and `OWNER` with the risk description and identified\\nowner. Repeat `--threatens ARTIFACT-ID` for each threatened artifact. Omit that\\noption if no affected formal artifact exists yet:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl raise-risk REPO --domain DOMAIN --title \\\"Risk title\\\" --description \\\"What could go wrong and why it matters\\\" --action \\\"Next follow-up action\\\" --owner OWNER --threatens ARTIFACT-ID --dry-run --json\\n```\\n\\nAdd `--with-decision` only if action 7 identifies a decision (DEC) that must\\nblock the named artifacts. Use the same option in both preview and creation.\\nA risk (RISK) alone does not block work.\\n\\n**Completion:** Identified risks (RISK) have formal records with an owner and\\nnext action. If none were identified, retain `None identified` with the\\nreviewed scope as transient working material.\\n\\n**Later use:** Review any paired decision (DEC) in [Record unresolved decisions (DEC)](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#record-unresolved-decisions-dec). [Prepare work orders (WO) linking the definitions, scope, planned work, and verification requirements](DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements) uses the\\nrisks (RISK) to define work and stop conditions and adds links that depend on\\nnew work order (WO) IDs.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"8431175790f8bf07019c19f9cb51d6ee5186b8bc66fccfbb2665ab99fc5028e9\"}, {\"heading\": \"raised-risks\", \"title\": \"Raised risks\", \"anchor\": \"raised-risks\", \"start_line\": 176, \"end_line\": 187, \"content\": \"## Raised risks\\n\\nA risk (RISK) in `raised` may have no paired decision\\n(DEC). Recording that risk alone does not block work. Use\\n`raise-risk --with-decision` when creating a risk that needs a paired blocking\\ndecision.\\n\\nA raised risk MUST NOT have more than one paired decision in `open` or\\n`deferred`. When that decision exists, it names the risk in `concerns`, and\\nits `blocks` set MUST equal the risk's `threatens` set. Disposing the paired\\ndecision applies its recorded effect to the risk in the same operation.\\nThe blocked artifacts change state only through their own transitions.\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"dcbef84857f6b71fbfa2099de79f6caa4d82e8977b13465eccb762ffc3a9ea1e\"}, {\"heading\": \"blocking-decisions\", \"title\": \"Blocking decisions\", \"anchor\": \"blocking-decisions\", \"start_line\": 150, \"end_line\": 175, \"content\": \"## Blocking decisions\\n\\nA decision (DEC) in `open` blocks every transition\\nof the artifacts in its `blocks` relation. A decision (DEC) in `deferred`\\nblocks transitions outside its recorded permitted scope.\\n\\nFor example, a decision (DEC) names work order (WO) `WO-EXAMPLE-001` in both\\n`concerns` and `blocks`. It is deferred with the scope\\n`WO-EXAMPLE-001:approved-in_progress`. This deferral\\nallows the work order (WO) to move from `approved` to `in_progress` if all\\nother checks pass. It still blocks moving that work order (WO) from\\n`in_progress` to `implemented`. The deferral also records when the decision\\n(DEC) must be revisited. Deferral does not itself start the work.\\n\\nAn accepted deviation is a decision (DEC) with `kind = \\\"deviation\\\"`,\\n`status = \\\"decided\\\"`, and `disposition.option = \\\"accept\\\"`.\\nIt records permission to depart from one identified specification (SPEC)\\nrule; \\u201caccepted\\u201d is not a separate lifecycle state for the decision (DEC).\\n\\nThat deviation remains applicable to the affected specification (SPEC),\\nwork orders (WO), and their verification records (VREC) and release records\\n(RLS) until a later decision (DEC) against the same rule reaches\\n`status = \\\"decided\\\"` with `disposition.option` set to `amend` or\\n`supersede`. The disposition is written through `harnessctl decide`, not\\nby editing the metadata by hand.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ed29cb785085f0704b9ab61f95ab42f2ee01579c0d191cb6587ce6c97684cdc0\"}, {\"heading\": \"links-for-decisions-and-risks\", \"title\": \"Links for decisions and risks\", \"anchor\": \"links-for-decisions-and-risks\", \"start_line\": 132, \"end_line\": 149, \"content\": \"## Links for decisions and risks\\n\\n| Source \\u2192 target | Relation | Meaning and coverage |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Decision (DEC) \\u2192 any artifact type | `concerns` | Names every artifact the question is about. |\\n| Decision (DEC) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ), Specification (SPEC), Verification contract (VER), Architecture (ARCH), Architecture decision (ADR), or Work order (WO) | `blocks` | Names artifacts whose transitions the decision (DEC) blocks. Each must also appear in `concerns`. |\\n| Decision (DEC) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ), Specification (SPEC), Verification contract (VER), Architecture (ARCH), Architecture decision (ADR), or Work order (WO) | `produces` | A decision (DEC) in `decided` names artifacts its answer created or amended, when applicable. |\\n| Risk (RISK) \\u2192 any artifact type | `threatens` | Names the artifacts the risk (RISK) could damage. |\\n| Risk (RISK) \\u2192 Work order (WO) | `mitigated_by` | Names the work orders (WO) reducing a risk (RISK) in `mitigating` or `mitigated`. The decision operation writes this link. |\\n| Risk (RISK) \\u2192 Architecture decision (ADR) or Decision (DEC) | `avoided_by` | Names the single architecture decision (ADR) or decision (DEC) that removes a risk (RISK) in `avoided`. The decision operation writes this link. |\\n\\nA decision (DEC) records a question that needs an answer or a proposed deviation.\\nAn architecture decision (ADR) records a settled design choice. They serve different purposes.\\n\\nA risk (RISK) does not block work by itself. When a blocking decision (DEC)\\nis requested, that decision (DEC) concerns the risk (RISK). The `blocks` set\\nof the decision (DEC) matches the `threatens` set of the risk (RISK).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"5009680651d50038248f4c60c5fceaf6065393bf7b3b2f370c54560ba83dd63a\"}]}]}",
  "is_error": false

Related work-order (WO) states do not change.\\n- **Retained files:** The generated evaluator evidence and candidate snapshot\\n  or export required by the capture procedure.\\n- **Transient working material:** The capture result and inspected output paths.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. If a suitable verification record (VREC) already exists, inspect it and\\n   continue to [Obtain the human's verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#obtain-the-humans-verification-decision). Do not duplicate an interrupted successful capture.\\n2. Confirm preparation authority under every selected work order's (WO)\\n   approval. Reuse it while the scope and inputs match.\\n3. Select an unused `VREC-ID` after checking the repository's local Git refs.\\n4. Confirm the domain and actual record and evidence destinations. Keep all\\n   generated writes within the authorized preparation scope.\\n5. Establish a clean committed candidate using authorized local Git actions.\\n   Retain its full commit ID. Do not discard unrelated changes to obtain it.\\n6. Run the capture command with each selected work order (WO), every declared\\n   verification contract (VER), and each retained evidence file.\\n7. Read the generated record and evaluator evidence. Confirm the candidate\\n   commit, selected IDs, evidence digests, and `ready` state.\\n8. Retain generated records and evidence in a later authorized governance\\n   commit. Preserve the earlier candidate commit that the record assesses.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl capture-verification REPO --id VREC-ID --work-order WO-ID --verification VER-ID --evidence EVIDENCE-PATH --owner ACTOR --domain DOMAIN --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact VREC-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nUse the actual preparation actor for `--owner`. Preparation does not record\\na future verification or release decision. Preserve the generated record and\\nits bound evidence without changing the recorded evidence bytes.\\n\\nRepeat `--work-order`, `--verification`, and `--evidence` for every selected\\ninput. `EVIDENCE-PATH` is a repository-relative file, not a directory or an\\nindex whose links will be followed automatically. Capture writes immediately\\nafter its checks; it has no `--dry-run` or `--apply` option.\\n\\nIf an unchanged rebase leaves an earlier ready record bound to the old\\ncandidate, use [Refresh verification after an unchanged rebase](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#refresh-verification-after-an-unchanged-rebase).\\nA verified source or changed relevant inputs cannot use that shortcut.\\n\\nIf preserving local edits requires the supported committed-candidate route,\\nuse `--candidate-commit COMMIT` with `--test-command EXECUTABLE ARGUMENTS`.\\nPut `--test-command` last. That route tests the named commit in a temporary\\ncheckout; use its actual results and returned record, not results from the\\nuncommitted edits.\\n\\n**Completion:** A ready verification record (VREC) binds the selected candidate\\nand evidence, or capture reports a specific refusal. Preparation is not verification.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Obtain the human's verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#obtain-the-humans-verification-decision) presents the exact record and evidence for the human decision.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"34e77e503346373221eaa0bb46e970ee738ce6a5eebbfdece9ba6e8ee36450a1\"}, {\"heading\": \"assess-the-verification-evidence\", \"title\": \"Assess the verification evidence\", \"anchor\": \"assess-the-verification-evidence\", \"start_line\": 70, \"end_line\": 107, \"content\": \"### Assess the verification evidence\\n\\n**Inputs:** The selected candidate, accepted definitions, verification\\ncontracts (VER), and retained implementation evidence.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Retained evidence files:** A requirement-by-requirement assessment with\\n  actual check results and unresolved gaps at the specified evidence locations.\\n- **Formal artifacts:** No verification decision or lifecycle transition.\\n- **Transient working material:** Review notes not required as retained evidence.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Compare the candidate's observed behavior with each acceptance criterion.\\n2. Map every required check to its actual evidence file and pass condition.\\n3. Confirm that the evidence applies to the selected candidate and environment.\\n4. Run missing checks using the verification contract's (VER) commands or\\n   manual procedure. Retain their actual results.\\n5. Record each criterion as passed, failed, or not assessed, with its reason.\\n6. Retain material findings and their resolution with the verification evidence.\\n7. For a defect requiring implementation changes, identify a work order that\\n   covers the correction and is eligible for execution. Follow the recovery\\n   rules under \\u201cIf a procedure is blocked.\\u201d A completed work order does not\\n   become executable again because verification found a defect.\\n8. After the authorized correction, establish the new candidate identity and\\n   reassess the affected criteria against evidence for that candidate.\\n\\n**Harness command:** None for the substantive assessment. Use the check\\ncommands and manual assessments defined in the verification contracts (VER).\\nHarness validation alone does not prove the required behavior.\\n\\n**Completion:** Every required criterion has evidence or a visible gap.\\nFailures and missing checks are not reported as passes.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Prepare the verification record](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#prepare-the-verification-record) binds the retained evidence to a verification record\\n(VREC). [Obtain the human's verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#obtain-the-humans-verification-decision) uses it for the human's assessment.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"78a405625bfb24107f4b8f4f09ad84942d5710c55b27d58f3114da5f40688c3b\"}, {\"heading\": \"record-the-verification-decision\", \"title\": \"Record the verification decision\", \"anchor\": \"record-the-verification-decision\", \"start_line\": 255, \"end_line\": 300, \"content\": \"### Record the verification decision\\n\\n**Inputs:** The exact human decision, ready verification record (VREC), and\\nunchanged candidate and evidence inputs.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Only the selected verification record (VREC) receives\\n  its permitted state and lifecycle-history entry.\\n- **Retained files:** The updated record is retained through authorized Git\\n  actions. Historical candidate and evidence facts are preserved.\\n- **Transient working material:** The observed decision result and next action.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Recheck that the selected inputs still match the human decision.\\n2. Preview the exact transition.\\n3. Apply the same command when its gates pass and effects match the decision.\\n4. Inspect the verification record (VREC) and resulting workflow context.\\n5. Report its actual state, any blocker, and the evaluator's next action.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set VREC-ID=TARGET --decision VREC-ID=ACTOR --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set VREC-ID=TARGET --decision VREC-ID=ACTOR --apply --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact VREC-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nFor supersession, select a successor verification record that is already\\n`verified` or `released` and preserves the old record\\u2019s work-order coverage.\\nUse the transition preview to assess that selection.\\n\\nFor `rejected`, add `--reason \\\"VREC-ID=Rejection reason\\\"` to preview and apply.\\nFor `superseded`, add `--reason \\\"VREC-ID=SUCCESSOR-VREC-ID\\\"` to both. Preserve\\nthe old record; do not rewrite its candidate or evidence to match a new result.\\n\\n**Completion:** The selected verification record (VREC) has the recorded\\ndecision. Referenced work orders (WO) and release records (RLS) remain unchanged.\\n\\n**Later use:** For PR-based work, [Publish the verification decision](PULL_REQUEST.md#publish-the-verification-decision)\\nas the final commit under the existing grant. Eligible verified coverage\\nsupports the selected delivery path.\\nA rejection or supersession follows the evaluator's remediation or selection\\nprocedure; it does not authorize new implementation scope.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"99e090908551d2012bdadac654496a2c14eefe9399b04112fcf067f6386854d7\"}]}]}",

  "content": "{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/RELEASE.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h44\\\\f\\\\claude-421\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\RELEASE.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"ce700f8f764c4425978f070d978d48eacafb927601f45e298c765f46dae90f7f\", \"bytes\": 7849, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"read-this-when\", \"title\": \"Read this when\", \"anchor\": \"read-this-when\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 6, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Read this when\\n\\nThe evaluator selects release-record preparation or a decision on a ready release record.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"6aca380f7ecb033e57e7e4bf6aca16914111bae9e93070270f93b5380517c210\"}, {\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nBefore preparing, read [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#release-coverage](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#release-coverage) and the selected REL/VREC records. Before a release decision, read [AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights](AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights) and [AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation](AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ddbc0b4cafdf1d5c05a185936aa8cb848c0028eeca29b9bc05ee6365782404b0\"}, {\"heading\": \"prepare-a-release-record\", \"title\": \"Prepare a release record\", \"anchor\": \"prepare-a-release-record\", \"start_line\": 13, \"end_line\": 71, \"content\": \"### Prepare a release record\\n\\n**Inputs:** The selected path, existing preparation authority, exact candidate,\\nand the release contract (REL) and eligible verified coverage required by that\\npath. Release-record preparation requires both.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Release path:** One release record (RLS) in `ready` and its generated\\n  evaluator evidence, when preparation is required and succeeds.\\n- **Retained files:** Required build or delivery evidence at the authorized\\n  locations. Builds occur only when separately covered by the selected scope.\\n- **Transient working material:** Preparation notes, proposed external content,\\n  and inspected write destinations.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Confirm authority for the exact preparation operation. Obtain a missing\\n   human decision before writing; reuse matching authority already supplied.\\n2. Inspect existing records and outputs before creating replacements.\\n3. For release, select an active release contract (REL), version, domain,\\n   and unused release record (RLS) ID. Check local Git refs and existing\\n   version reservations before choosing the ID and version.\\n4. Select the final eligible verification record (VREC) for the candidate.\\n   Its work-order (WO) set must exactly cover the work being released.\\n5. Confirm all intended output paths and the clean working-tree condition\\n   required by release preparation.\\n6. Run the release preparation command. Inspect its written record, evidence,\\n   candidate identity, and `ready` state.\\n7. Retain the new release record (RLS) and evidence in an authorized governance\\n   commit after the candidate they describe.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nFor release preparation:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl prepare-release REPO --id RLS-ID --release-contract REL-ID --verification-record VREC-ID --work-order WO-ID --version VERSION --owner ACTOR --domain DOMAIN --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact RLS-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nUse the actual preparation actor for `--owner`. Preparation does not record\\na future verification or release decision. Preserve the generated record and\\nits bound evidence without changing the recorded evidence bytes.\\n\\nRepeat `--work-order` for every released work order (WO). This evaluator requires one final verification record (VREC) covering the complete\\nrelease. Earlier records remain supporting evidence. If that coverage is\\nmissing, return to verification instead of inventing or relabelling it.\\n\\nAdd `--tag TAG` only for an explicitly selected tag value; this records the\\nvalue and does not create a Git tag. `prepare-release` writes after its checks;\\nit has no `--dry-run` or `--apply` option.\\n\\n**Completion:** The required delivery inputs are prepared, or a precise\\npreparation blocker is known. Preparation performs no merge, publication,\\ndeployment, or release decision.\\n\\n**Later use:** A ready release record (RLS) proceeds to [Obtain the release decision, when required](RELEASE.md#obtain-the-release-decision-when-required). \\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"d3fcc6f4d9565acc0d714479b8b27df0173ce927ec4d36a757bf1f5710f34942\"}, {\"heading\": \"record-the-release-decision-when-required\", \"title\": \"Record the release decision, when required\", \"anchor\": \"record-the-release-decision-when-required\", \"start_line\": 117, \"end_line\": 159, \"content\": \"### Record the release decision, when required\\n\\n**Inputs:** The human's exact decision and unchanged release inputs.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Only the selected release record (RLS) receives the\\n  permitted state and lifecycle-history entry.\\n- **Retained files:** The updated release record (RLS), retained through\\n  authorized Git actions.\\n- **Transient working material:** The applied result and current next action.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Compare the current release inputs with the human's reviewed inputs.\\n2. Preview the selected transition.\\n3. Apply the same command when its gates pass and effects match the decision.\\n4. Inspect the release record (RLS) and report the actual resulting state.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set RLS-ID=TARGET --decision RLS-ID=ACTOR --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set RLS-ID=TARGET --decision RLS-ID=ACTOR --apply --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact RLS-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nFor rejection, add `--reason \\\"RLS-ID=Rejection reason\\\"` to both transition\\ncommands. Related verification records (VREC) and work orders (WO) are not\\ntransitioned automatically.\\n\\nFor a complete-release decision, use the existing `--reason` input to retain the\\nactual human decision reference and reviewed delivery-plan path and SHA-256.\\nThis is retained evidence of the supplied decision, not permission derived by\\nparsing arbitrary reason text. Preserve the referenced plan bytes for each later\\nauthority comparison. No new approval file or lifecycle state is needed.\\n\\n**Completion:** The release decision is recorded or explicitly refused.\\nNo Git tag, publication, or deployment has been performed by this transition.\\n\\n**Later use:** A released record may support [Confirm authority for the external action](DELIVER_RESULT.md#confirm-authority-for-the-external-action)'s external-action checks.\\nRejection follows the evaluator's remediation procedure.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"41884593e91b2762c5d0406d1b6e73f0f7731edf06676a4cf15a64b0760c789d\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/DELIVER_RESULT.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h44\\\\f\\\\claude-421\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\DELIVER_RESULT.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"13405ba32a2227a5c20abb59e806de18ed60b4ecf3c010508f053587cd8bf6b2\", \"bytes\": 12123, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"read-this-when\", \"title\": \"Read this when\", \"anchor\": \"read-this-when\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 6, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Read this when\\n\\nA delivery path is selected or its exact external action needs preparation, authority or readback.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ead6dc699ad51b30b9deca478ada5107ea915cf305c8d2365602961d48f68d2e\"}, {\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nBefore any external action, read [AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights](AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights) and the repository instructions for that action. Read the exact selected candidate, verification or release record.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"088b0023cee60e9d78ebb2916dd2db983e71274c32128f7d0e8f6d4144535b62\"}, {\"heading\": \"select-the-delivery-action\", \"title\": \"Select the delivery action\", \"anchor\": \"select-the-delivery-action\", \"start_line\": 43, \"end_line\": 79, \"content\": \"### Select the delivery action\\n\\n**Inputs:** The requested delivery, selected work or verification record,\\ncandidate identity, and intended destination.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** None changed.\\n- **Transient working material:** One named action, its exact candidate or\\n  release identity, destination, selected procedure, and required authority.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Inspect the selected work order (WO), verification record (VREC), or release\\n   record (RLS) with the command below.\\n2. Name the action: for example, create a pull request, merge, prepare a\\n   release, tag, publish, or deploy.\\n3. Identify the full candidate commit or immutable release identity.\\n4. Identify the exact target repository and ref, registry, or deployment environment.\\n5. Read the repository's instructions for that delivery action.\\n6. Select the matching procedure or a complete alternative declared by the\\n   evaluator. Resolve an ambiguous destination with the requester.\\n\\n**Harness command:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact ARTIFACT-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nUse a work order (WO), verification record (VREC), or release record (RLS)\\nas `ARTIFACT-ID`. Selection changes no lifecycle state.\\n\\n**Completion:** One delivery action and target are explicit. Selecting a path\\ndoes not authorize or perform its external action.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Prepare the delivery package](DELIVER_RESULT.md#prepare-the-delivery-package), [Obtain the release decision, when required](RELEASE.md#obtain-the-release-decision-when-required), [Record the release decision, when required](RELEASE.md#record-the-release-decision-when-required), [Confirm authority for the external action](DELIVER_RESULT.md#confirm-authority-for-the-external-action), [Perform the authorized delivery](DELIVER_RESULT.md#perform-the-authorized-delivery), [Confirm the delivery result](DELIVER_RESULT.md#confirm-the-delivery-result) prepare, authorize, perform, and confirm that action.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"3c62d9982634dc649143dfbaa6d84299d868a5b1f9f4d18861c99d673da2f01d\"}]}]}",

A successful shape check alone never supplies an admission decision.\n273\t\n274\tA lost response, evaluator process crash or ambiguous database commit is not an\n275\taccepted or refused receipt. The client reports transport uncertainty and uses\n276\toperation lookup or an identical retry. A 404 lookup alone cannot prove that a\n277\tconcurrent transaction rolled back. A known precommit failure leaves no effects;\n278\tan unknown commit must be reconciled against the authoritative operation store.\n279\t\n280\t## Scenario and schema qualification\n281\t\n282\t`tests/hosted_artifact_graph/fixtures/scenarios-v1.json` maps all twelve\n283\tVER-HAG-001 cases to explicit positive/failure outcomes and storage support. Every\n284\thosted execution entry is `unperformed`. Its wire examples contain synthetic\n285\tidentities and demonstrate shape only; their apparent receipt values are not\n286\tobserved acceptances. The original fixed canonical vectors remain unchanged.\n287\t\n288\tFor independent shape qualification, install `jsonschema==4.26.0` in a disposable\n289\tenvironment and run its Python against:\n290\t\n291\t```text\n292\tpython -I -B tests/hosted_artifact_graph/validate_wire_contracts.py\n293\tpython -m unittest tests.test_hosted_artifact_graph\n294\t```\n295\t\n296\tThe first command registers the three local schemas without network resolution,\n297\tvalidates fixed vectors and the complete source manifest, and exercises accepted\n298\tand rejected shapes. It does not introduce a core runtime dependency. The second\n299\tcommand checks fixed bytes and digests through the existing test entry point.\n300\tNeither command executes service admission, transactions, Cypher or recovery.\n301\t\n302\t## Physical representation\n303\t\n304\tProject stores identity, schema revision and the integer command guard. Artifact\n305\tstores project-scoped identity. Revision stores its canonical `envelope_json`,\n306\t`document_base64`, artifact ID, raw document digest and derived type/status.\n307\tBaseline stores `manifest_json`; its SELECTS edges are derived from that manifest.\n308\tDraftContext stores base baseline, selected work order, version and proposals.\n309\tOperation stores project/principal/key, semantic request digest and immutable\n310\t`result_json`. JSON text properties retain exact machine structures without\n311\texpanding scalar fields into graph nodes.\n312\t\n313\tHAS_REVISION links Artifact to Revision. SELECTS links Baseline to Revision.\n314\tBASED_ON links DraftContext to Baseline. PROPOSES links DraftContext to Revision\n315\twith the selected artifact ID. DECLARES links Revision to the target Artifact,\n316\twith `kind` and `target_artifact_id`; resolve the target revision through the view.\n317\tCross-project edges, duplicate selections, and edges inconsistent with canonical\n318\tcontent fail import/export checks. Unresolved authoring placeholders remain\n319\texplicit findings and cannot become invented valid target nodes.\n320\t\n321\tThe public Cypher surface uses the selected project's Artifact and Revision\n322\tnodes, its selected Baseline (or context/base), and the corresponding storage\n323\tedges above. Project exposes only project ID, schema revision and the observed\n324\tcommand version. Artifact exposes project/artifact IDs. Revision exposes its IDs,\n325\ttype, status, document digest, envelope JSON and document base64. Baseline exposes\n326\tits IDs and manifest JSON. DraftContext exposes its IDs, selected work order,\n327\tbase baseline and context version. DECLARES exposes kind and target artifact ID;\n328\tPROPOSES exposes the selected artifact ID. Other edge properties are not public.\n329\t\n330\tOperation nodes and their result JSON are private to command handling and the\n331\tprincipal-scoped operation lookup. They are not available through Cypher. A\n332\tquery cannot use internal labels/properties, an unselected revision, another\n333\tbaseline/context, or caller-authored project filters to widen this surface. The\n334\tservice must apply that projection before query execution and use the same\n335\tread-only transaction snapshot for selection and results. This is application\n336\tadmission; it does not resolve RISK-HAG-001 or prove database privileges.\n337\t\n338\t`graph-v1.cypher` supplies six composite/single uniqueness keys, key/content\n339\texistence constraints and explicit lookup indexes. Memgraph requires separate\n340\tindexes for uniqueness constraints ([official constraint documentation](https://memgraph.com/docs/fundamentals/constraints)).\n341\tSchema creation must be an explicit operator step on an empty store; later\n342\tstartup verifies it and refuses mismatch. Explicit initialization, stored revision\n343\tmismatch and missing-index refusal have now been tested for the exact candidate\n344\tin the [qualification report](../engineering/hosted-artifact-graph/evidence/WO-HAG-001/phase2-20261005/protocol04-assessment.md).\n345\t\n346\t## Deferred boundary and historical qualification\n347\t\n348\tCypher remains part of the sandbox: parse a narrow read grammar, constrain the\n349\tselected view, apply row/byte/depth/time limits and roll back the read transaction.\n350\tDatabase-enforced read-only access remains RISK-HAG-001; no authoritative-pilot or\n351\tpublic-service claim is made. The current contract does not authorize a parser\n352\tbypass, a replacement lifecycle policy or suppression of malformed input.\n353\t\n354\tThe candidate now includes its dependency lock, image/Compose files, admission\n355\tadapter, transaction implementation, remote client and plugin guidance. The\n356\tpackaged-client walkthrough, live concurrency and refusal checks, independent\n357\tevaluator comparison and restart/restore have passed for candidate\n358\t`7290af984337e122b193981a187e58c29de41a16`. The linked report preserves earlier\n359\tfailures and exact component identities.\n360\t\n361\tThe [later Claude qualification](../engineering/hosted-artifact-graph/evidence/WO-HAG-001/claude-20261006/report.md)\n362\tuses candidate `5fa50787dba1fdd010f625335d844416dd3bf002`. Authentication works;\n363\tthe corrected MCP schemas allow all seven native tools. The guided CLI sequence,\n364\tHTTP/MCP response comparison and repeated live boundary suite pass. Claude still\n365\tmisreported a large partial response as complete. A smaller follow-up was correctly\n366\treported; it does not erase that failure.\n367\t\n368\tThe [Codex continuation](../engineering/hosted-artifact-graph/evidence/WO-HAG-001/codex-20261006/report.md)\n369\ton that same candidate completes 18 installed-client operations and seven native\n370\tMCP reads, with exact HTTP parity and correct partial-result reporting. It retains\n371\tthe original wheel-access and MCP approval-policy failures. The successful runs\n372\tuse the normal host profile and approval reviewer; no persistent permissions were\n373\tweakened. Exact candidate guidance was read explicitly, so automatic plugin loading\n374\tand desktop remain unobserved. Earlier restart/restore and evaluator results above\n375\tremain historical candidate04 evidence. WO-HAG-001 remains in_progress, and PR #535\n376\tremains draft.\n377\t\n378\t\n379\t## Current Phase 2 qualification\n380\t\n381\tThe [current assessment](../engineering/hosted-artifact-graph/evidence/WO-HAG-001/final-20261006/report.md)\n382\trecords all twelve required scenarios for the final candidate, its exact component\n383\ttuple, real native CLI observations and restart/restore. It preserves the earlier\n384\tfailures above. Large saved MCP responses expose their completeness metadata to\n385\tbounded file reads. Parser failures preserve their errors without returning an\n386\tunusable catalog that exceeds the CLI response bound.\n387\t\n388\tThe assessment distinguishes tested behavior from human verification. Read the\n389\tlinked work orders and verification record for current lifecycle state. Codex\n390\tcandidate guidance was read explicitly; automatic loading and desktop were not\n391\ttested. Database-side read-only enforcement remains RISK-HAG-001. Phase 3 pilot\n392\tauthority and Phase 4 production/release obligations require later work.\n393\t\n394\t## Authoring cost and candidate guidance\n395\t\n396\tWO-HAG-011 adds typed file inputs and compact evidence-backed results to the\n397\texisting client. See [the concrete interface](harnessctl-reference.md#concise-hosted-authoring).\n398\tSkills route hosted drafting, lifecycle rehearsal and repository work separately.\n399\tThese candidate changes require their own tests; earlier service qualification\n400\tdoes not establish improved task duration or context use. Git remains authoritative.\n401\t"
